articles.title: 2026 Mr. Olympia Live Updates, Highlights and Reaction From Night One
articles.summary: Everybody has a favorite Ms. Olympia winner, right?
articles.body:
Everybody has a favorite Ms. Olympia winner, right?

Sure, we'll concede many people's memories stall after Rachel McLish and Cory Everson—who combined to win eight of 10 titles from 1980 to 1989—but another buff female has joined their ranks.

The 2026 Ms. Olympia crown was won (again) by Andrea Shaw, stretching a run to seven in a row dating back to 2020.

The finals were held at the Orleans Arena in Las Vegas after morning pre-judging at the Las Vegas Convention Center.

The Wellness and Classic Physique competitions are the final two on Friday's agenda.

Derek Lunsford, Samson Dauda, Andrew Jacked and Nick Walker were the final four callouts for the Men's Open (Mr. Olympia) division in Friday's pre-judging session.

It doesn't guarantee a top-four finish, however, because Friday's judging is worth 50 percent of the final score, as is Saturday's final judging.

Lunsford and Dauda were alongside each other for all of the final session, initially in the middle of the quartet and later with Dauda on one side of the stage and Lunsford immediately to his right.

"Derek has a very good tan," analyst Phil Heath said. "With his skin texture he's looking very polished."

Six athletes were among the initial callouts for Men's Open (Mr. Olympia) pre-judging, including Derek Lunsford and Samson Dauda, who've combined to win the last three titles.

The half-dozen athletes went through a series of poses as called out by event judges.

Dauda and Lunsford, who've been vocal rivals beyond the stage, too, were positioned alongside each other for the final portion of the posing session.

Two-time Mr. Olympia champ Derek Lunsford is in the Friday night pre-judging mix while chasing a third "Men's Open" division title in the last four events.

Lunsford won the 2023 show in Orlando and got his second win last year in Las Vegas.

Lunsford and 2024 winner Samson Dauda were among the final athletes to do an individual pose routine for pre-judging. Lunsford, 33, was born in Indiana and has been a professional bodybuilder since 2017. He won the 212 Olympia division title in 2021.

Dauda, 40, was born in Nigeria and has lived in the United Kingdom for more than 20 years. He challenged his competitors to a pose-down during a pre-competition press conference, but Lunsford refused.

Friday night's biggest prize has been awarded, but the event is not over.

Athletes involved in pre-judging for the Mr. Olympia competition, whose finals are on Saturday night, followed the Ms. Olympia contestants to the stage.

Take your pick. But both apply to Andrea Shaw on Friday night.

The 42-year-old who grew up in Michigan continued a Ms. Olympia dynasty at the Orleans Arena with her seventh straight victory, besting a field of nine other finalists including repeat second-place finisher Ashley Lynette Jones.

Also finishing in the top five were Brazil's Leyvina Barros, Finland's Paula Ranta and Megan Morrison from West Virginia.

An emotional Shaw dedicated the show to her mother, who was unable to attend the event due to illness.

Wrapping up the 10-woman posing series is six-time defending Ms. Olympia champion Andrea Shaw.

Brazilian Leyvina Barros was the first of 10 finalists to pose for the Ms. Olympia title. She was third in 2025.

And now it's the "women's bodybuilding" division, whose winner is crowned Ms. Olympia.

Keone Pearson acted like a three-time champion.

The 31-year-old seized the center of the stage during a group pose down with four other finalists, engaging each in a one-on-one flex-off and dominating every time on the way to a fourth straight win in the Men's 212 Olympia division.

Pearson won a $50,000 check by outpointing a finalist field that included Lucas Garcia, Shaun Clarida, Vitor Alves Porto De Oliveira and Nihat Kaya.

"This year I just locked myself in a cage and pretended like I'd never won anything," Pearson said. "That gave me something to chase."

The men are getting a turn on the Friday night stage with the 212 Olympia division, which is reserved for athletes who weigh no more than 212 pounds.

Lola Montez climbed the most important rung on the Figure division ladder, moving from 2025 runner-up to 2026 champion.

Montez was second to Rhea Gayle in 2025.

Wondering what goes into making an Olympia champion in the Figure division? Wonder no more.

Judges focus, among other things, on an athletic, feminine physique with a sharp V-shape, ideal shoulder-to-waist ratio, and moderate conditioning.

The first title of the weekend was awarded shortly after 9:45 p.m. ET when Natalia Abraham Coelho emerged from a field of nine called to the center of the stage in the Women's Physique division.

The win was her third in a row and she also picked up a check for $50,000.

Competitors went through required poses in a series of callouts—first in a group of five women followed by a group of four. A trimmed down field of five was called one at a time for individual poses set to selected music, like an Olympic free skate.

Finally, the top-five finishers were called out together for a pose down to music.

Former Mr. Olympia competitor Bob Cicherillo is the master of ceremonies at a cavernous Orleans Arena and he tried to pump the crowd in predictable fashion by labeling the event as the "Super Bowl of bodybuilding."

Twelve women have won the Ms. Olympia title since the initial competition in 1980. Six of those women have multiple titles.

Iris Kyle holds the record with 10 wins, followed Lenda Murray with eight and both Cory Everson and Andrea Shaw with six.

Shaw has won six in a row, matching Everson's run from 1984 to 1989 and Murray's run from 1990 to 1990. Kyle won in 2004, then won nine straight from 2006 to 2014.

In addition to other criteria, athletes qualify to compete on the Olympia stage by finishing within the top 25 of the season point standings for divisions that use a points-based qualification system.

Also, former Olympia winners hold lifetime eligibility, though entry must be approved if it's been more than five years since their last victory.

In addition to crowning a Ms. Olympia for 2026, the Friday finals will also reveal winners in the Figure Olympia, Women's Physique Olympia and Wellness Olympia divisions.

The top four heading into Friday's Ms. Olympia finals after prejudging are Leyvina Rodrigues Barros, Ashley Lynnette Jones, Paula Ranta and Andrea Shaw.

Shaw is the reigning champion and has six titles in a row dating back to 2020.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 3 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice
articles.summary: Check out Justin Boone's full list of sits and starts for Week 3.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 3 rankings.

Coming off a four-touchdown effort versus the Bills last Thursday, Goff returns to the fast track at Ford Field for a potential shootout with the Jets.

The Lions defense has been hit hard by injuries and will force their offense to keep attacking most weeks. That's great news for fantasy managers, since Detroit is loaded with high-quality skill position players who will benefit from inflated stat lines.

Detroit has the fifth-highest implied point total of the week (27) and Goff has traditionally been better at home. He's comfortably inside my top-10 QBs this week.

Kyler Murray at Buccaneers – Murray is out of concussion protocol and facing a Tampa defense that's been struggling so much, they just let Deshaun Watson finish as a top-12 fantasy QB in Week 2.

Tyler Shough vs. Raiders – Shough was a top-eight fantasy QB in each of the first two games, in part thanks to Kellen Moore's fast-paced offense. While I'd like to see him not rely as much on fourth-quarter stats, there's no denying his fantasy value at this point.

Hubbard was already looking like one of the best fantasy picks of the year, even before Jonathon Brooks was sent to injured reserve for at least six weeks. Now there's no serious competition for touches — with AJ Dillon serving as the new backup.

It might seem like we're walking a fine line with Hubbard only getting 13 and 14 touches in the first two weeks, but he's been extremely effective, totaling 151 scrimmage yards, five catches and three touchdowns so far.

The Panthers offense is humming and another positive game script awaits against a Cleveland defense that's allowed 88 yards to Bhayshul Tuten and 90 yards to Bucky Irving . Hubbard is a high-end RB2 in this matchup who most managers were able to get in the middle rounds.

Breece Hall at Lions – The Lions defense gave up over 100 scrimmage yards to Travis Etienne Jr. and Kendre Miller in Week 1, then let James Cook III post 139 yards last Thursday. Meanwhile, Hall looks healthy and is playing some of his best ball in a while, with 210 yards and a score through two games.

David Montgomery at Colts – Indy's defense has been hemorrhaging fantasy points to running backs, allowing Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker to top 160 scrimmage yards each. Montgomery may not be on their talent level, but he should have a solid day with the Texans favored on the road.

Quinshon Judkins vs. Panthers – After tough matchups on the road against the Jaguars and Bucs, Judkins gets a Panthers defense permitting the most fantasy points to his position. It's now or never for the second-year back.

Zay Flowers is trending towards missing another contest due to the hamstring aggravation he suffered in Week 1. Though Flowers travelled with the team to Brazil, it would be surprising if he suited up.

In his absence last week, Bateman led the team with nine targets, which he turned into seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown.

We've seen these kinds of spike weeks from Bateman before, only for him to turn back into a fantasy pumpkin, but I'm hopeful he can repeat that success in a game with the highest projected point total of the week at 53.5.

Tee Higgins at Steelers – Higgins has feasted on the Steelers defense during his career, averaging over 70 yards and nearly a TD per game across his last four meetings with them.

Tetairoa McMillan at Browns – With Jalen Coker dealing with an ankle injury, McMillan will be the healthiest Panthers wideout on Sunday. Cleveland is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to receivers through two weeks.

Deebo Samuel Sr. vs. Cardinals – Deebo has nine catches and two carries on the season and is somehow one of the healthier members of the 49ers receiving corps. The 49ers are tied for the second-highest implied point total (28).

Nico Collins is likely going to miss another game with a hamstring injury, putting Schultz in position to lead the Texans in receiving once again.

Not only did the veteran tight end see a stunning 14 targets in Week 2, he caught 12 of them for 140 yards. There just aren't many tight ends who have that kind of volume in their range of outcomes.

It also bodes well that the Colts just allowed a 9-101-1 stat line to another slower veteran tight end Travis Kelce . Start Schultz confidently as a top-10 option this week.

Terrance Ferguson at Broncos – Puka Nacua doesn't seem likely to play this week, so Ferguson will have a chance to replicate his 54-yard, one-touchdown effort from last week. Ferguson has scored four touchdowns in his young career and they've all occurred in games where either Nacua or Davante Adams missed.

Mark Andrews at Cowboys – The Ravens are one of the teams tied for the second-highest implied point total (28). Bateman can't catch all the passes and the Cowboys are the seventh-best matchup for fantasy tight ends so far.

It's been a slow start to the season for Nix, who has finished as the QB31 and QB18 in the opening weeks. A date with the Rams doesn't seem like the spot where he'll find his rhythm.

After stumbling their way through the Australia game and losing Myles Garrett to IR, the Rams defense rebounded in Week 2 with Aaron Donald rejoining the club.

Even oddsmakers aren't buying into the Broncos this week, making them 2.5-point underdogs at home with an implied point total of 21.5.

Matthew Stafford at Broncos – Stafford had a terrible outing versus the 49ers and a great showing against the Giants. Unfortunately for him, the Broncos defense carries a degree of difficulty much closer to the Niners matchup. Puka Nacua will be missed in this contest if he can't go.

Baker Mayfield vs. Vikings – The Buccaneers offense is discombobulated at the moment, so much so that Baker wasn't even able to capitalize on a revenge game versus the Browns last week. Facing Brian Flores' Vikings defense is the opposite of a get-right spot.

TreVeyon Henderson /Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots

After being one of the toughest matchups for fantasy running backs last year, the Jaguars have picked up where they left off by holding every back they've encountered so far to less than 40 rushing yards.

Though Stevenson's fumbling issues popped back up last week and led to an increased workload for Henderson, we'll likely see this remain a fairly even split. So don't expect volume to save the day for either of these backs.

Henderson's explosiveness gives him a chance to hit one big play at any time, like we saw last week on his 39-yard TD run. However, plays like that are extremely rare against Jacksonville 's front.

Travis Etienne Jr. vs. Raiders – Etienne's usage has been puzzling, being stuck in a three-man committee each of the first two games. He's also been limited in practice so far this week with a hamstring injury. If you're starting him, you have to understand the risks by now.

J.K. Dobbins vs. Rams – Despite an injury scare last week, Dobbins somehow emerged as the healthiest Broncos runner. RJ Harvey is also expected back from his hamstring injury for this game, while rookie Jonah Coleman is now in danger of missing with an ankle issue. Even so, Dobbins has only managed 36 rushing yards in each of the first two outings, with no targets and no touchdowns.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt vs. Seahawks – The Commanders just lost the engine of their offense in Jayden Daniels and now have to take on the ferocious Seahawks defense. JCM hasn't looked bad as the lead back this year, but this isn't the spot to play him for fantasy.

Stefon Diggs/Terry McLaurin, WR, Commanders

Speaking of the Commanders, we have to downgrade their entire offense this week. Even though Marcus Mariota can give them 60-70% of what Jayden Daniels did, the loss of their franchise quarterback completely changes how defenses prepare for this attack.

While they might eventually settle in with Mariota under center, that's not going to happen this week against a Seahawks defense that's allowing the fewest fantasy points to receivers.

Diggs will be startable in other weeks, but he's a risky TD-or-bust flex option in this contest. McLaurin's outlook is even murkier after he struggled last season when Daniels was out of the lineup.

Luther Burden III/Rome Odunze vs. Eagles – Few teams can support multiple fantasy players when they're starting their third-string quarterback, who in this case is Case Keenum . However, Burden and Odunze weren't putting up big numbers even when Caleb Williams was playing. Don't panic sell; just send them to your bench until Caleb returns.

Courtland Sutton vs. Rams – Sutton has posted two catches for 11 yards in the opener and three grabs for 25 yards in Week 2. Now he gets the Rams and 49ers over the next two games. Despite being 79% rostered in Yahoo leagues, you can drop him without hesitation.

Brian Thomas Jr. vs. Patriots – Thomas hasn't topped 40 yards in a game this season and the Patriots have held every receiver they've faced aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to 35 scoreless yards or less. BTJ is a boom-or-bust WR4/flex who's unlikely to boom versus New England .

It doesn't matter where you drafted him; you can't play Loveland right now. After giving you zero fantasy points in the opener, he managed just one catch for three yards in a rain-soaked loss to the Vikings.

It's shocking results for a player who was a target hog down the stretch and into the playoffs last year, but it's the current reality. The situation is only made worse with Case Keenum expected to start.

On top of it all, the Eagles have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to tight ends, holding everyone at the position to 16 yards or less. Send Loveland to the bench and we'll reassess in better matchups when Caleb Williams is healthy.

Harold Fannin Jr. vs. Panthers – Fannin got more involved in a good matchup with the Bucs last week, but the Panthers have been much tougher on tight ends this year. With Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion providing real target competition, Fannin is more of a TE2 streamer.

Brenton Strange vs. Patriots – New England was the sixth-hardest matchup for tight ends last year and has carried that over as the fourth-worst opponent for the position this season. Meanwhile, Strange has been held to 23 yards and 17 yards in his first two outings.

articles.title: ‘I know I’m going to be important’ – Dani Olmo not worried by lack of Barcelona starts
articles.summary: The forward has only started three games this season.
articles.body:
Dani Olmo says he's not worried about his lack of starts this season for Barcelona as he knows there is plenty of football to be played and that he "will be important."

The Spain star has started only three times this season and has been asked how he feels about the situation in a new interview with La Vanguardia.

"Yeah, I'm fine. The season is very long; I know I'm going to be important and that's how I feel," he said. "We had time off and Flick has been dosing the minutes at Barça, rotating a lot. I feel very good and ready for everything."

"Yeah, I'm fine. The season is very long; I know I'm going to be important and that's how I feel," he said.

"We had time off and Flick has been dosing the minutes at Barça, rotating a lot. I feel very good and ready for everything."

Olmo also spoke about his form at the World Cup and how he wants to replicate that with his club side.

"It is true that in the World Cup I felt very good and I made good matches, a great tournament," he added. "That level is the one I want to show at Barça. I have had some episodes of little continuity, but I have been very well, and I think I can still contribute much more to my game, both with the team and with Barça. That's my goal. "In the end, the systems are different. In Barça we have more premises to fulfill because the attack is a little more positional, within a certain freedom. "Here, in the selection, we are given more freedom to change positions and move. Neither better nor worse, they are different ideas, and in both I find myself perfectly. I think this year I have started in a very good way and I want to continue adding."

articles.title: 4 Lakers on hottest trade candidate seats entering 2026-27 NBA training camp
articles.summary: Following the Los Angeles Lakers’ offseason in which they revamped the roster around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, they sit at 16 standard contracts on the...
articles.body:
Following the Los Angeles Lakers ' offseason in which they revamped the roster around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves , they sit at 16 standard contracts on the roster heading into the start of training camp next week. That's one over the league maximum of 15, requiring the Lakers to identify potential trade candidates.

At some point between now and the start of the regular season, the Lakers are going to need to cut the roster down to at least 15 standard contracts. During a preseason press conference on Thursday, general manager Rob Pelinka acknowledged the roster crunch, while addressing the timeline for making a potential trade.

"The spirit of competition has been great, and to some extent, going from 16 guys to 15 guys, we have until opening night for the competition to play out and see who the best 15 players are," Pelinka told assembled media. "Behind that evaluation of who is emerging in camp, there's also consolidation trades that can still be looked at, trading two guys out, bringing one in. So there's a number of ways that could be addressed, and the back end point of it will be before we play the Warriors . So the next month will kind of answer those questions."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

As Pelinka said, training camp could play a role in deciding who those trade candidates are for the Lakers, but here's a breakdown of the initial names that could find themselves in a different uniform come the start of the regular season.

When the Lakers traded Deandre Ayton to the Washington Wizards in the offseason, they received Jaden Hardy in exchange, but the real prize for the team was the two second-round picks they acquired in the deal. Hardy has been a borderline rotation player during his career, and has been more on the out than in, in recent seasons.

He did play well for the Wizards last season in a 23-game stretch after being moved at the deadline, but overall he doesn't fit the Lakers' offseason goals of getting more athletic and versatile defensively as free agent signees Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle do. And while he's only 23-years-old, he certainly isn't as much of a development priority as Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr.

Hardy's main attraction for potential trade partners is his expiring contract. He's under contract for this season, and then he has a team option on his deal for 2027-28. Aside from that, perhaps another team might want to take a flyer on a relatively young guard who can provide instant offense off the bench, but not much else. In any case, he doesn't appear to be long for LA whether it's a trade, or declining his option at the end of the year if they can't move him.

Jarred Vanderbilt's name has come up in trade rumors over the past year, most recently during the rumored offseason talks between the Lakers and Atlanta Hawks regarding a potential sign-and-trade involving Jonathan Kuminga .

Vanderbilt still fits the Lakers' roster in the sense that he's among their most versatile defensive players, and he will always bring 100 percent energy, even if it does go overboard at times. But with the signings of Williams and Thybulle, that seems to squeeze him out of the bench rotation, of which he already was on the edge of last season.

One of the biggest hinderances to trading Vanderbilt is his contract . He still has this season on his deal, and then a player option for 2027-28, giving him more control over his future than whatever team he might be on. He's still capable of helping a team, but his contract combined with his recent injury history probably causes teams to pause. Plus getting a team to agree to take him might cost the Lakers some draft capital and they probably aren't too keen on that. Nevertheless, he is still a prime candidate to be moved eventually.

Dalton Knecht actually was traded at the 2024-25 deadline, to the Charlotte Hornets before the Lakers withdrew from the deal over concerns regarding Mark Williams ' health. After the rescinded trade, Knecht was never able to regain the confidence and momentum he built in the early months of his rookie season.

Ever since then, his name has seemingly come up in trade rumors, but the Lakers have not yet moved him. He had chances last season to reintegrate himself into the rotation, but was unable to seize the opportunity. He's still on his rookie deal, and the Lakers have already picked up his option for this season, but he's an expiring contract too in the sense that he has another team option for 2027-28.

The deadline to pick up Knecht's option for next season is Oct. 31. If not, he will hit unrestricted free agency in the offseason. And while he was an older rookie, there is the chance that another team is still intrigued with what he showed early that season, and believes a change of scenery could unlock that again. Expect to hear his name come up as the Lakers' deadline to trim the roster gets closer.

One of the Lakers' main offseason acquisitions last offseason, LaRavia started out his tenure in the purple and gold as a rather solid role player, before his play tailed off as the season went on, and then into the playoffs. If he can regain the form he showed early last year, he is still serviceable for this team. He's a hard-nosed forward who can defend and shoot the 3-ball, and can act as a connector offensively.

But with the acquisition of Sandro Mamukelashvili , along with Williams and Thybulle, LaRavia also appears to potentially be squeezed out of the rotation. Depending on what happens during training camp and preseason, he could find himself on the outside looking in.

He's an expiring contract as well. He's in the final year of a two-year deal he signed last summer. And he still theoretically provides valuable production on the court. His name hasn't come up as much in trade rumors as the above mentioned players, but certainly could become a prime trade candidate for the Lakers.

articles.title: Jon Gruden Questions Steelers’ Offensive Line Chaos Amid Struggles: ‘Why?’
articles.summary: Jon Gruden has seen plenty of offensive lines during his coaching career; however, the Pittsburgh Steelers’ current setup has left him genuinely puzzled. The...
articles.body:
Jon Gruden has seen plenty of offensive lines during his coaching career; however, the Pittsburgh Steelers' current setup has left him genuinely puzzled. The former head coach watched the unit shuffle players between positions through the offseason and into the regular season, and now the results are becoming harder to ignore.

The Steelers entered the year hoping their offensive line would settle into a reliable group. Instead, the Steelers are still moving pieces around while quarterback Aaron Rodgers continues to take pressure behind them. After a rough Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots , Gruden has a simple question about the whole approach: Why keep changing it?

Jon Gruden Questions Pittsburgh Steelers ' Offensive Line Shuffle

The Steelers have already dealt with plenty of changes up front this season. Zach Frazier is the only starter who remained at the same position from last year, while Troy Fautanu moved from right tackle to left tackle, and Mason McCormick switched from right guard to left guard.

Gruden addressed the situation w hile discussing the Steelers' Week 3 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals . The constant movement stood out to him, especially with the Steelers already having trouble protecting Rodgers and opening holes in the running game.

"The offensive line has been one of the most incredible things that I've ever seen this year. There has been more movement on this offensive line than any line I've ever seen. They're all playing different positions this year. I'm like, 'Where the hell's my left tackle? Oh, he's at right tackle. Where's my right guard? Oh, he's over there.' A lot of mix-and-match going on, and I think that has a lot to do with the funk that they're in. I'm just here to wonder, why?"

Dylan Cook went from playing left tackle last season to starting at right tackle. Spencer Anderson , who had been a swing tackle, moved into the starting right guard spot. The changes were intended to create a new combination; however, the unit has struggled to find much consistency.

The Steelers gave up four sacks and seven QB hits in their 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Their running game hasn't offered much help either. The Patriots also exposed some of the communication problems that can arise when a group is still learning to play together. New England head coach Mike Vrabel used six-man pressures to create confusion, and Rodgers was hit hard as Pittsburgh failed to sort them out.

The Steelers had been hoping the line would grow into a strength, particularly after investing heavily in the position through the draft. Fautanu is a former first-round pick, while the organization has spent other premium draft capital on the unit in recent years.

Except the Steelers are heading into Week 3 with more questions than answers. The Bengals now become the next test , and the Steelers don't have much time to sort things out. If the line continues to struggle, the focus will naturally return to the decision to change so many positions in the first place.

articles.title: 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa will miss a few games after hurting his calf
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa injured his calf warming up for practice earlier this week and will miss a few games.  Coach Kyle Shanahan sai...
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa injured his calf warming up for practice earlier this week and will miss a few games.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said that Bosa got hurt before practice on Thursday doing "high knees." Shanahan said Friday that the injury wasn't believed to be long term but he would likely miss a few weeks starting with Sunday's game against Arizona .

The injury is the latest to hit the defensive line for the 49ers, who are missing seven players at the position this week, including Mykel Williams who is still working his way back from knee surgery last year.

Defensive end Sam Okuayinonu broke his foot just before the Niners left for the season opener in Australia and is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. Defensive tackle Alfred Collins went down with a season-ending knee injury in practice in Australia.

Defensive tackle C.J. West was placed on injured reserve this week after undergoing surgery for bone chips in his knee and fellow defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. has been ruled out for at least a few weeks after leaving last week's game with a high ankle sprain.

Rookie defensive end Romello Height had surgery on a broken hand this week and will also miss this week's game.

This is the third straight season when the Niners have dealt with a high number of injuries.

"You get used to just dealing with it," Shanahan said. "Lots of people have to go through stuff in this league all the time, some worse than others. I know we haven't had good luck these last couple of years. It started out bad, so hopefully we're getting it out of the way and it'll get better as the year goes. I'm happy that we haven't lost those guys for the whole year, but you just plug away and look on to the next challenge."

The loss of Bosa would be the most significant on the defensive line as the Niners were hoping he would be healthy this season after going down with a season-ending ACL injury in Week 3 last year.

Bosa has looked solid the first two weeks even though he hasn't had a sack. He had five pressures in Week 1 against Miami , according to Pro Football Focus, and has elevated a defense that finished last in the NFL with 20 sacks last season.

"He's been really the most dominant player without a sack," defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said Thursday. "I have to say he's been awesome."

Bosa has had at least nine sacks in the five seasons when he didn't get hurt in the opening month as he has been one of the most productive edge rushers ever since being drafted second overall in 2019.

Bosa has made the Pro Bowl in all five of his healthy seasons and won the AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year award in 2022, when he led the league with 18 1/2 sacks.

Bosa's 74 1/2 sacks in the regular season and playoffs are the fifth most in the NFL since he entered the league in 2019 despite missing nearly two full seasons. His 280 total pressures rank fourth most in the NFL in that span, according to Sportradar.

Receiver Mike Evans was listed as questionable for the game with a hip injury. He returned to practice Friday on a limited basis.

articles.title: Royals vs Guardians, September 25 live game discussion
articles.summary: It’s Denny’s 8000th!
articles.body:
Today is my penultimate game thread for the 2026 MLB Regular season. You might have noticed I've been using that word a lot lately. You've probably guessed it's my favorite word. You're right.

Last time we were together, Noah Cameron was performing his penultimate start to the season. Today is the ultimate. It would be swell if he performed that colloquially as well as definitionally and did something crazy like pitch a no-hitter. The Guardians clinched a playoff berth last night. Perhaps they're too hungover to hit? They don't add asterisks for that, though, so Cameron should try to take advantage.

The Guardians are still battling for an opportunity to win the division rather than simply to make a playoff berth. They currently lead the White Sox by a single game in the standings, but the White Sox hold the tiebreaker, so all it will take is for Chicago to win a single game more than the Guardians do this weekend for them to claim the division crown. I'm hoping the Royals sweep the Guardians and make it easy for them. Still, the point I'm taking forever to get to is that Gavin Williams gets the start for Cleveland rather than preparing himself for a playoff series, because if the Guardians can hold out, they won't have to play in the Wild Card series anyway.

By the numbers, Gavin has been terrific this year for Cleveland. Eating innings with style. If you dig a little deeper, you find that he is nearly elite at generating both chase and whiffs. One interesting note to me is that he has universally struggled a bit when hitters actually make contact with any of his pitches. He mixes up his pitches well, so rather than hunt a particular pitch, the Royals might be best served just trying to make contact with whatever he throws and hope for the best.

Williams has faced the Royals twice this year. In their first series, he tossed 5.2 innings of 1-run ball and struck out 8. But he also walked 5, which contributed to the short outing. He took the loss in their second meeting during the second series between the two teams, giving up 5 runs in 6 innings, though he only walked 2 and struck out 7. The Royals managed to sequence really well in that game, scoring those five runs on only eight hits with a pair of doubles and a pair of dingers.

It's kind of funny that Isaac Collins got left out of tonight's lineup. He's been unplayably bad for a bit now, but the last time the Royals faced Williams, he had a home run and a double in a 3-for-3 effort. Still, this is probably the best lineup the Royals can put together with their current roster. You could argue that Michael Massey should be above Salvador Perez , or that Nick Loftin should start in left and shift John Rave to center to bench Kyle Isbel . That would all be nitpicking, though. Hopefully the Royals can bring Denny Matthews a win for his 8000th broadcast!

articles.title: International team lead US in Presidents Cup
articles.summary: The International team produce a brilliant fightback in the foursomes on day two of the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead over the United States.
articles.body:
The International team produced a brilliant fightback in the foursomes on day two of the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead over the United States.

The US had been 3-2 up after the fourballs on Thursday but in a stunning turnaround were beaten in all five matches in the alternate-shot format in Medinah on Friday.

It boosted their hopes of a first victory in the event since 1998 and only a second since the competition began in 1994.

Geoff Ogilvy's side secured their first point of the day as Sungjae Im and Hideki Matsuyama saw off Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman 3&2.

Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor then produced a stunning result as they held on to beat world number one Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns by one hole.

Burns almost snatched a half when his 20-foot putt at the last lipped out.

Open champion Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee also edged a see-saw contest with Collin Morikawa and Wyndham Clark by one hole, before Adam Scott and Christiaan Bezuidenhout defeated Justin Thomas and Cameron Young 3&2.

Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim wrapped up the day with a dominant 4&3 victory over Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele.

There will be four further foursomes matches and four more fourballs on Saturday, with 12 singles games taking place on Sunday.

articles.title: Game Thread: Rockies (57-102) at White Sox (82-77)
articles.summary: South Siders likely need a series sweep to claim the division title
articles.body:
Well, well, well what do we have here? The same Chicago White Sox team that blew a six-run lead just last week has now roared back to life, winning four of its last five. Unfortunately, the Cleveland Guardians are still selling their souls to win every game they play, but that streak will eventually run out … right?

Either way, the White Sox have a three-game homestand to end the season against the worst team in baseball. If they can manage a sweep and the Kansas City Royals can avoid one of their own, the division is ours. Granted, the division would be already wrapped up if the White Sox hadn't mostly sleepwalked through September, but what are you going to do?

The South Siders have clinched a playoff spot after years of despair, and now the ball is in their court to end the season on a high note. Standing, or more acting as a traffic cone in their way, are the Colorado Rockies . To put it simply, the Rockies are pathetic and their pitching staff is the worst in the majors by a wide margin. It's not a surprise for a franchise that's been struggling for relevance since 2018, and the Rockies have looked like they've wanted to go home since the All-Star break if we're being honest.

All that lines up for a golden opportunity for the White Sox, but we've seen this all before. Let's not get ahead of ourselves and make sure the guys who are now likely extremely hungover can get the job done.

Starting for the Colorado Rockies is Tomoyuki Sugano , who may be the most confusing pitcher in history. He has a 5.36 ERA but an 12-11 record for a 102-loss team. He's gone winless in his last seven starts, with six losses and an ERA over eight. Somehow, in the eight games before that, he had a ERA of more than 5 yet went 6-1 over that stretch.

For as bad as Sugano has been lately, he did give up just one hit and one run in his last outing against the Seattle Mariners . Somehow, the Rockies play well when he pitches, so this isn't the "easy win" it should be on paper.

As for the White Sox, they are throwing out Sean Burke . Burke has been a stud for most of the season and while his record (3-1) over his last seven starts has been solid, his ERA of more than five has left plenty to be desired. Thanks to their own actions, the margin for error for the White Sox is nonexistent, so Burke will need to be sharp so the White Sox can get ahead early.

This is usually the part where I make a prediction and say what I think is going to happen, but I truly don't know any longer. This team looked dead to rights after one of the worst blown leads I've seen in a while just last week, but somehow they've picked themselves up off the mat.

This Chicago team is just as likely to lose by 10 as they are to put up 20 runs, so I might as well just say to tune in. If it's like any of the previous 159 games, it'll be an entertaining game one way or another.

Now, would somebody PLEASE beat the Guardians?

articles.title: Sean Payton pleased with performance of Evan Engram and Nate Adkins thus far
articles.summary: Tight ends Evan Engram and Nate Adkins have each had an impressive performance early on in the 2026 season.
articles.body:
One area the Denver Broncos hope to improve upon this season is the impact their group of tight ends make on offense. Last year, the group failed to impress and didn't make a lot of big plays through the air. Instead of pursuing a major addition in free agency, the Broncos opted to run it back with most of their players at the position.

A big free agent signing during the 2025 offseason, Evan Engram wasn't the 'joker' player the team thought he would be last season. Though in his first two games of his 2026 season with the squad, Engram has made the most of the opportunities that have gone his way.

Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton pointed out that he was impressed with how Evan Engram was doing early on this season in his second year with the team.

"He's doing well. He's had a catch in each game, there's some things he gives you in the passing game, and I think he's blocking well, so I'm excited for him. I think he's shown, especially in regard to protections and certain things, he gives you that threat. He's doing well within the role," stated Payton.

Last season, Engram caught 50 passes for 461 yards and just 1 touchdown. Those were some of the lowest production totals in his NFL career. In two games, Engram has caught five of six targets for 60 yards and a touchdown with four of those receptions moving the chains for a first down.

Payton also remarked that he was impressed with the work Engram had put in over the offseason and training camp to improve his blocking. In turn, that has led to more reps on the field and involvement in helping in the run game. Thus far, the ten-year veteran has been on the field for 57-percent of Denver's offensive plays—a fifteen percent jump from 2025.

In addition to Engram, Payton is pleased with what third-year tight end Nate Adkins has achieved. Third in Denver's trio of tight ends behind Adam Trautman and the aforementioned Engram, Adkins has been a versatile player for Denver's offense and is looking to rebound after missing almost half of last year due to injury.

Thus far, he has been a key blocker to kickstart Denver's rushing attack. Moreover, he recently flashed as a safety outlet for quarterback Bo Nix . Last week in their comeback victory over the Jaguars, Adkins had a quality performance. He hauled in three receptions on three targets for 32 yards and a touchdown.

Since signing with the Broncos as an undrafted free agent in 2024, he has been an underrated player in the team's offensive endeavors. Payton noted the aforementioned, but also his special teams' abilities as something that has stood out to him early on making him a valuable member of the team.

"He does a lot of things well. He can play in the kicking game; he blocks well. I don't want to use the word Swiss Army Knife, but he's one of those guys where once you describe the assignment, he's really good blocking in space. You see some of that carry over into the kicking game."

Over the course of the season, the Broncos will need Engram and Adkins to continue to be quality contributors. With Jaylen Waddle in the fold, there will be less targets to go around for Denver's tight end group, but if they can maximize the opportunities that come their way like they have thus far, the offense should be a lot more consistent than they were a season ago.

articles.title: WWE SmackDown Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights From September 25
articles.summary: Before we head to Chicago for Worlds Collide this weekend, WWE made a stop by Indianapolis for this week's SmackDown.
articles.body:
Before we head to Chicago for Worlds Collide this weekend, WWE made a stop by Indianapolis for this week's SmackDown.

Here's a look at what WWE advertised for Friday's show:

CM Punk vs. Gunther vs. Finn Balor (MITB Qualifier)

Charlotte Flair vs. Giulia vs. Lash Legend (MITB Qualifier)

Fatal Influence vs. Chelsea Green, Paige and Tiffany Stratton

Trick Williams vs. Baron Corbin (United States Championship, Steel Cage)

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's SmackDown.

Last time in action: Trick Williams defeated Baron Corbin (SNME, September 6)

When the USA Network went live in the arena about 10 minutes before the show started, Randy Orton interrupted Michael Cole and said he is going to interview him before the end of the show. It then suddenly cut back to a commercial and the end of the show that aired before SmackDown.

When the show finally started, we saw the cage being lowered for the United States Championship match between Williams and Corbin. Cole called this the final chapter of their story.

They started the match with a flurry of punches, so there was no wasting time with lockups or headlocks. Trick Willy was the first to take control, but Corbin used the cage to his advantage.

This has been a hot and cold feud, but Corbin and Williams have developed good chemistry as opponents. They clearly know each other's strengths, and the fact that they have a lot of physical similarities makes it an even contest.

Cage matches used to be a big attraction in WWE, but these days, it can feel more restrictive than anything else. There is only so much you can do with the cage, so giving fans anything fresh is almost impossible. That being said, this wasn't a bad match.

Corbin played a great bully, and Williams had the crowd behind him whenever he had the upper hand. This match won't set the world on fire, but it was a decent way to get the show started with something other than a talking segment.

Corbin kicked the cage door into Lil Yachty's face at ringside, but it came back to bite him when Yachty slammed it back in his face as he tried to escape. Williams was able to put him away to retain the title in the end.

Putting something semi-interesting in that little pre-show segment was a nice change of pace. It's usually just a shot of the crowd.

The sound completely cut out about 30 seconds before the first commercial break.

The superplex from the top of the cage was a cool spot.

Charlotte Flair vs. Giulia vs. Lash Legend

Last time in action: Giulia lost to Michin (Main Event, August 14), Legend won a tag match with Nia Jax (SmackDown, August 24), Flair lost a six-woman tag (SNME, September 6)

The second match of the night was another women's MITB qualifier with Giulia, Flair and Legend fighting for one of the remaining spots.

Legend came into this bout with the biggest power advantage, and Giulia was definitely the underdog due to her size, but the nature of a triple threat match evened the playing field and made it feel like any of them could win and it would be believable.

This was a pretty typical three-way. We got to see every combination one-on-one, and we saw several moments that included all three competitors. They did a good job making it feel less predictable than a lot of matches, but there wasn't much to it overall. It was a solid match that gave all three women some good moments.

Flair being the only former world champion of the three made her the easy choice, as well as the predictable choice, so the more interesting outcome was either of the two other woman winning. Thankfully, that is exactly what happened.

The final few minutes were the best part of the match. Legend ended up spoiling the win for Giulia and hitting her finisher to qualify for MITB.

Result: Legend defeated Giulia and Flair

Paige, Chelsea, Nikki and Tiffany had a backstage segment. Nikki vowed to win the title from Chelsea.

The fact that WWE hasn't done more with Giulia is a travesty. She is one of the best workers they have.

The modified Tower of Doom spot looked good. They had a unique setup instead of the usual suplex.

Michael Cole sat backstage with Randy Orton for the interview Orton forced him to do. Cole said he wasn't sure what to do, so Orton asked him about his interview with Cody Rhodes last week.

Orton did almost all of the talking. He spoke about Rhodes and what he has done in his career. He claimed Cody has changed many times in his career, but Orton said he has always been the same person.

The Viper said he wants that 15th championship, and if he has to go through Rhodes to get it, then he will.

The way this segment started was great. Cole felt uncomfortable, and Orton felt like he might snap at any moment. As the interview went on, Orton got louder and angrier, but he stopped feeling like he might attack Cole, which took some of the intensity away from the proceedings.

Blake Monroe vs. Giulia was booked for next week during a backstage segment. If the match actually happens, it will be a miracle.

Chelsea Green and Tiffany Stratton and Paige vs. Fatal Influence

Jacy Jayne. Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley took on Green, Stratton and Paige in a six-woman tag match this week.

This bout featured every champion in the SmackDown women's division, but the only thing on the line was bragging rights.

Reid is still early in her career, but the other five women have all established themselves as talented performers, so this match had some fun moments sprinkled in.

Green, as usual, was especially entertaining. She has carved out a rare niche for herself as someone who can be both a comedic wrestler and somebody WWE can rely on for a strong in-ring performance. The crowd loves her, and she seems to be able to adapt to any opponent.

This wasn't a high-stakes match, but that almost worked to its advantage because either team could have won and nobody would bat an eye at it.

This wasn't the most exciting match of the night, but the crowd was enjoying it, and everyone put in a good effort. Nikki Bella showed up and interfered, which allowed Jayne to pin Paige for the win.

Result: Fatal Influence defeated Green, Stratton and Paige

Fatal Influence will face three stars from AAA at Worlds Collide tomorrow in Chicago.

Green is the funniest champion in WWE right now. She barely has to try and she is still hilarious.

Last time in action: Balor vs. Gunther vs. Owens ended in a No Contest (SmackDown, August 24), Punk lost to Sami Zayn (SmackDown, Sept. 11)

Cody Rhodes came to the ring to talk about what is going on with Orton, as well as his quest to regain the WWE title. As he was leaving, Punk made his entrance for the main event against Balor and Gunther for a spot in the MITB match.

Gunther went after Balor as soon as the bell rang, but Punk was not about to be ignored and threw himself in the fight.

Unsurprisingly, this was the best thing on the entire show. Punk was good, but Gunther and Balor were the interesting combo. It feels like WWE is building a singles feud between them. They focused on each other more than Punk in this match.

Everyone got a chance to come close to winning before Punk stole the win from Balor by covering Gunther right after he hit the Coup de Grace. The final few minutes were especially enjoyable.

Punk and Rhodes shared a long look as they passed each other in the aisle.

Balor needs to bring the Demon character back again. It really set him apart from everyone else.

The two-man Boston crab on Gunther was a fun spot.

Friday's SmackDown was an eventful episode. We got a steel cage match for the U.S. title, a couple of MITB qualifiers, and a few segments that advanced various feuds.

Was this the strongest episode of SmackDown? Not by a long shot, but it was a decent way to spend a couple of hours on a Friday night.

Punk, Balor and Gunther stole the show, but Williams and Corbin kicked the night off with a cage match that the crowd seemed to enjoy.

Money in the Bank is always one of the most interesting PLEs of the year because WWE has the chance to give someone surprising a push with the briefcases. Let's hope this year's winners make the most of the opportunity.

articles.title: 'Not too much pressure': How Zhu Jiner turned struggles in India into taking China closer to Chess Olympiad gold | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad is currently edging towards its climax in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad is currently edging towards its climax in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. In the women's section, one team has pulled clear of the rest, and it is China, the comfortable leaders at the moment. And if anything doesn't go south, it will be the Chinese girls donning the gold medals around their necks at the end of 11 rounds of play. But do you know the most interesting thing in it? China don't even have their strongest players in the event.As per the current FIDE ratings, none of the world top three, which include Hou Yifan, the current women's world champion Ju Wenjun, and Lei Tingjie, is part of this Chinese side. Zhu Jiner, the world no. 4, is thus on Board 1, facing the toughest of the top board opponents at this Samarkand Olympiad. And she has risen to the challenge, remaining unbeaten throughout, a complete turnaround from her form at the Global Chess League (GCL) in India just a couple of weeks earlier.Just before the Olympiad, Jiner was part of the two-time GCL champion Triveni Continental Kings, who had a torrid event as they finished second from bottom in the group stage this time. Jiner's performance was not up to the mark either, with the 23-year-old Grandmaster winning just one, losing four and drawing five games in the tournament.The on-board results, coupled with the hectic schedule, meant little time or urge for her to enjoy the city of Bengaluru, the host of this fourth edition of GCL.Finding warmth amid a difficult campaignDespite her struggles on the board, Jiner maintained a deep appreciation for the host nation. "This is my first time in Bengaluru, and overall, I’ve had a very good impression of the city. The weather is also very pleasant," Jiner told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction."Since I’m here mainly to compete in the Global Chess League, there’s been quite a lot of time spent on matches and preparation, so I haven’t really had much time to go out. When I have a game, most of my energy is focused on the competition."Bengaluru was simply the latest stop in Jiner’s long-standing relationship with Indian chess venues, having previously played across the country's major hubs."I’ve been to India several times before. I’ve visited New Delhi, Pune, Mumbai, and now Bengaluru, all for international chess tournaments," she recounted. "What I like most about India is how passionate people are about chess. Whether they’re players or fans, you can really feel their love for the game. For example, during this Global Chess League, the players have received such a warm welcome from the local fans. Every day, when we come out of the playing venue, there are so many chess fans waiting to get autographs or take photos with their idols. That atmosphere has left a very deep impression on me."Jiner also noted the broader cultural and competitive ties between the two Asian superpowers, acknowledging the explosive growth of Indian chess talent on the global stage."I think India has a very long and rich history and culture. I’ve heard some Indian mythological stories as well," she observed. "At the same time, India is a very vibrant and rapidly developing country, and there is a lot of trade and exchange between the two countries (India and China). As far as modern chess is concerned, India has developed incredibly quickly over the past few years, especially when it comes to the younger generation. There are now many very talented young Indian players, and they have achieved excellent results in international competitions again and again."From four-year-old beginner to China’s Board 1Jiner's journey to leading China's national team on Board 1 in Samarkand was built on decades of steady progression. "I was introduced to chess when I was about four years old. At first, it was very simple, I just thought the game was interesting and enjoyed playing it," Jiner recalled."Then, when I was around seven, I joined the Zhejiang team and began receiving more systematic training. Later, I joined the national team and gradually started competing at higher and higher levels. Actually, there wasn’t one particular moment when I suddenly decided, 'I want to become a professional chess player.' It happened gradually. Over time, chess became a very important part of my life, and eventually becoming a professional player felt like a natural choice for me."Her personal trajectory mirrors the unique structure of Chinese chess. "Chess came to China relatively late. It has been around for many years now, but compared with some other sports, it is still a relatively niche sport," Jiner explained."I’m not very familiar with the current development system for young Chinese players, but I think for a little girl who is just starting to learn chess, the most important thing is to first develop a genuine love for the game. The professional path is actually very long, and there will be many difficulties along the way. If you really love the sport, that’s what will help you keep going."Steering the ship in SamarkandThat resilience proved essential as China arrived in Samarkand without its standard contingent of World Champions. Leading an understrength team, Jiner reframed the narrative, turning the absence of superstars into a source of resolve."I think China has some of the strongest female players in the world, and overall, the team has consistently been among the strongest," Jiner noted before the start of the tournament. "However, this time, the Chinese team hasn’t been able to compete at the Olympiad with its most complete and strongest lineup, which I personally feel is a little unfortunate."Rather than letting the pressure of top-board responsibility overwhelm her squad after the setback in India, Jiner embraced the lowered expectations, which has worked well for her and her team so far.ALSO READ: Juggling Chess Olympiad prep and a commentary gig in India: The other side of USA's only female GM Irina Krush"Of course, even under these circumstances, the Chinese women's team is still a very strong team. But there are many strong teams at this Olympiad, and I think the competition between them will be extremely intense. So I wouldn’t consider China the biggest favourite to win the title. For us, that actually means there isn’t too much pressure. We’ll prepare carefully for each round, focus on the opponent in front of us, try to play at our best, and aim for a good result."Jiner may not have considered China the biggest favourite to win the title. But that pragmatic, round-by-round focus is now on the verge of delivering one of the most remarkable gold medal runs in modern Olympiad history.(Indian women's team takes on China in the penultimate round of Chess Olympiad on Saturday.)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tim Tebow said Friday he is “pausing his relationship” with Life Surge, a Christian organization that’s been accused of using predatory sales tactics to exploit its followers’ faith and financial insecurity.
articles.body: Tim Tebow said Friday he is “pausing his relationship” with Life Surge, a Christian organization that’s been accused of using predatory sales tactics to exploit its followers’ faith and financial insecurity. Tebow, the 2007 Heisman Trophy winner who is currently a college football analyst with ESPN’s SEC Nation, said his team is conducting an internal investigation. He spoke on campus in advance of the Mississippi-Florida game at Florida Field on Saturday. “The allegations are extremely, extremely serious, and it’s something that we take very serious,” Tebow said. “So, for us, we’re having our team do an investigation, but also pausing our relationship ‘til we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more.” Tebow said he was “caught off guard” by the “Pablo Torre Finds Out” podcast that focused partly on Tebow’s speaking engagements with Life Surge. “I was at an anti-human trafficking conference (Thursday), and my team shared (it) with me when we were leaving as we were flying to Alabama for the event, and kind of caught off guard with some of it,” Tebow said. “I think that’s why I’m really trying to understand more of the facts to really learn it.” His message to his loyal followers amid the allegations: “It’s really important to get answers to understand every bit of that,” he said. “My heart … was to be able to share something that I love to share, which is the love of Christ and the good news of the gospel. And so I think it’s really important that we can really understand all the facts and details of it.” The podcast’s investigation raised questions about Tebow’s knowledge of the organization’s practices. Life Surge, which hosts around 30 events annually, typically brings in Christian celebrities like Tebow to headline events. At Life Surge’s one-day events, attendees are urged to sign up for impact classes that pitch packages ranging from $10,000 to $40,000, according to the podcast. If attendees can’t afford the price tag, Life Surge reportedly connects them with third-party lenders who encourage them to apply for credit cards or take out home-equity loans, according to the podcast. Life Surge has denied any wrongdoing, according to the podcast.

articles.title: Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve voices support for the trans community again after regular season finale vs Fever
articles.summary: Cheryl Reeve says her "Trans Kids Belong" shirt sparked an outpouring of messages from transgender families during a season defined by debate.
articles.body: Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve again voiced support for the transgender community Thursday, as competing rallies over trans athletes in women's sports raged outside her team's game for the third time this season. Reeve addressed the issue after Minnesota closed the regular season with an 86-66 victory over the Indiana Fever at Target Center. The remarks marked at least the fourth time this season that Reeve has discussed transgender issues during a WNBA media session. "I think that’s probably one of the more meaningful things that would mark the season for me," Reeve said. "It’s that the transgender community is one that deserves our support, and what is happening in the name of some issues of transgender in sports — it’s really an attack on all transgender community. They don’t want transgender people to exist." FORMER VIKINGS CAPTAIN JACK BREWER CALLS OUT LYNX COACH CHERYL REEVE FOR 'TRANS KIDS BELONG' SHIRT Reeve previously wore a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt during the Lynx’s previous home game against Indiana on Aug. 2. That game came shortly after Fever guard Sophie Cunningham publicly supported keeping biological males out of women’s and girls’ sports. "Save Women's Sports" activists then held another rally in support of Fever star Sophie Cunningham outside of the Target Center for the second time this season on Thursday, again prompting pro-trans counterprotesters. A similar rally took place outside of the Lynx's game against the Golden State Valkyries on Aug. 19. During the Aug. 2 game between the Lynx and Fever, Reeve and Cunningham were seen speaking at midcourt before that contest. Reeve later said the two understood they had platforms and shared an interest in educating people despite disagreeing on the issue. Reeve said Thursday that wearing the shirt was a "small gesture," but messages from transgender people and their families made it one of the most meaningful moments of her season. "The amount of communication of people who were affected by something as simple as wearing a T-shirt in support of them and helping them be seen — with the platform that we have in professional sports, it was a small gesture by me," Reeve said. "It’s something I believe in, obviously, wholeheartedly." "If I could have helped just one to feel differently about themselves, because for the transgender community this really is about life and death for them," she continued. "The number of parents of transgender kids that I heard from and how it helped them and their families, it helped their child think differently about themselves and that there is someone in our position, like we have as a leader. To know that there are people out there that believe in them, that they belong." WNBPA ISSUES STATEMENT EMBRACING DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION AMID TRANS ATHLETE DEBATE IN WOMEN'S SPORTS Reeve first addressed the subject during a July media availability following the Supreme Court’s rulings upholding state laws restricting transgender participation in women’s sports. She called the political focus on the issue "sort of sickening" and said "exclusion is never the answer." She returned to it before the Lynx’s Aug. 2 meeting with Indiana, when a rally supporting Cunningham’s position was held outside Target Center. Reeve defended the demonstrators’ right to assemble but rejected the argument that transgender athletes represented one of the most pressing problems facing women’s sports. "Every kid has a right to sports, regardless of gender diverse, transgender," Reeve said at the time, while acknowledging that eligibility questions become more nuanced after puberty. Following the game, Reeve addressed her conversation with Cunningham and reiterated her belief that transgender children should have access to sports. She also said activists focusing on transgender participation were overlooking other obstacles facing female athletes, including inadequate facilities, uniforms and locker rooms. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Cunningham has maintained that her position is not rooted in hatred. "I think that I am here to extend love," Cunningham previously said. "But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men." The debate prompted the WNBA to convene discussions with team leaders during the season. The league said there were no immediate transgender eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, while maintaining that fairness, competitive integrity and inclusion were among its priorities. No transgender woman has played in the league. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Minnesota finished the regular season with a league-best 33-11 record after Thursday’s victory. Indiana fell to 28-16 and entered the playoffs as the No. 6 seed.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: India’s 44-year wait ends as Sawan Barwal wins silver in men’s marathon
articles.summary: Sawan Barwal scripted history at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday, winning silver in the men’s marathon and ending India’s 44-year wait for a
articles.body: Sawan Barwal scripted history at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday, winning silver in the men’s marathon and ending India’s 44-year wait for a medal in the event. He clocked a personal best of 2:11:37, finishing 48 seconds behind Japan’s Ichitaka Yamashita, who won gold in 2:10:49. China’s Peiyou Feng took bronze with 2:12:13.The marathon started at 4 a.m. IST with 19 runners, including Barwal and fellow Indian Kartik Karkera. Barwal quickly established himself among the leaders and was in second place at the halfway mark with a timing of 1:05:54. He continued to hold his position as the race entered its final stages, reaching the 35-kilometre mark in second.With around seven kilometres left, Barwal was still chasing Yamashita. The Japanese runner eventually opened up a gap, but Barwal maintained his pace and stayed firmly in silver-medal position. He finished with a timing of 2:11:37, securing India’s first Asian Games marathon medal since the 1982 Delhi Games and the country’s first medal in the event on foreign soil.Historic medal for Indian athleticsThe silver adds to Barwal’s growing record. In April, he broke Shivnath Singh’s 48-year-old national marathon record at the NN Marathon Rotterdam. His latest performance now converts that record-setting form into a major international medal.Barwal’s silver is India’s fourth Asian Games marathon medal. Chhota Singh won gold and Surat Singh Mathur took bronze at the inaugural 1951 Games, while Hosur Kukkappa Seetharan won another bronze in 1982.The other Indian runner, Kartik Karkera, finished 17th among 19 competitors with a time of 2:22:41.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “I heard a voice, think about your wife and kids”-How Tyson Fury survived one-pound birth, mental health crisis and rose again to boxing champion
articles.summary: Tyson Fury’s life story goes far beyond boxing. Born three months premature and weighing just one pound, he survived when doctors feared he would not.
articles.body: Tyson Fury’s life story goes far beyond boxing. Born three months premature and weighing just one pound, he survived when doctors feared he would not. Years later, after beating Wladimir Klitschko and reaching the top of heavyweight boxing, Fury faced a very different fight. Depression, alcohol and drug use pushed him into a crisis so deep that he once drove his Ferrari towards a bridge at high speed. His wife, Paris Fury, his family and professional help became important parts of his return. Fury eventually rebuilt his life, returned to boxing and began speaking openly about mental health.How did Tyson Fury survive after being born weighing just one poundTyson Luke Fury was born on August 12, 1988, in Wythenshawe, Manchester. He arrived around three months early and weighed only one pound. His father, John Fury, had already experienced the loss of two daughters who were born prematurely, making Tyson’s survival even more uncertain.John later explained why he gave his son the name Tyson. Mike Tyson was the heavyweight champion at the time, and John believed the tiny baby would have to fight from the moment he was born.That belief became part of the family story around Tyson Fury. He grew up in an Irish Traveller family and later turned to boxing, eventually becoming one of the most recognised heavyweight fighters in the sport.His early life did not guarantee the career that followed. Fury had to build himself as a boxer before he could become a world champion. In November 2015, he travelled to Germany and beat Wladimir Klitschko on points, taking the WBA, IBF and WBO heavyweight titles. The WBO records the victory as Fury becoming a unified heavyweight champion.The success, however, did not bring the peace many people might expect.What happened to Tyson Fury after he defeated Wladimir KlitschkoFury’s problems became public after the biggest win of his career. He struggled with severe depression, gained a large amount of weight and turned to alcohol and cocaine. In 2016, the World Boxing Association recorded that a psychologist had confirmed his clinical depression. Fury later gave up his titles while dealing with his problems.He also spoke openly about how difficult that period had become. In an interview with The Joe Rogan Experience, Fury described driving a new Ferrari towards a bridge in 2016 while thinking about ending his life.He said: “I got the car up to 190 miles an hour and I was heading towards that bridge.”Fury said he then heard a voice telling him to think about his children and family. He pulled the car over and later decided he would not try to take his own life again. His account of the incident has been reported for years as one of the darkest moments of his struggle.The important part of the story is what happened after that night. Fury did not simply return to the gym and forget what had happened. He began dealing with the problems that had taken him so low.In 2018, he told BBC Sport that he had reached a point where he did not want to wake up, but had come back from that period. He also spoke about wanting his comeback to give hope to other people dealing with mental health problems.How did Paris Fury support Tyson Fury through his darkest yearsParis Fury was part of Tyson Fury’s life long before he became a world champion. The pair met as teenagers at a wedding. Paris was 15 and Tyson was 17 when they first met, and they later began a relationship before marrying in 2008.Their relationship also went through the hardest period of Tyson’s life. Paris has spoken about how his depression, alcohol problems and other struggles affected their family. She was not simply watching a famous boxer struggle from the outside. She was dealing with the same difficult period at home.That makes her role in Fury’s comeback different from the image of a celebrity partner standing beside a champion after a big fight. Paris knew Tyson before the belts, fame and money. She knew the person behind the boxer.Fury has repeatedly spoken about the importance of his family when discussing his darkest period. His own account of the Ferrari incident shows how strongly thoughts of his wife and children were tied to his decision to stop.The couple now have seven children. Their family life has also become part of the public story around Fury, but the most important part of Paris’s role came during the years when his career and personal life were both under serious pressure.How did Tyson Fury turn his mental health battle into a comeback storyFury eventually returned to boxing after more than two years away. He had lost a huge amount of weight, returned to training and began rebuilding his career step by step.His comeback became especially powerful because it was not only about winning fights. In December 2018, Fury faced Deontay Wilder for the WBC heavyweight title. In the 12th round, Wilder knocked Fury down, but Fury somehow got back to his feet before the final bell. The fight ended in a draw.That moment became one of the clearest images of Fury’s comeback. He had already spent years trying to rebuild himself outside the ring. Now he was doing the same thing in front of a huge audience.Fury later beat Wilder in their second fight in 2020 and stopped him again in their 2021 trilogy fight. He also retained the WBC title against Dillian Whyte at Wembley in April 2022, with 94,000 people attending the event.His mental health work also continued outside boxing. Fury worked with Campaign Against Living Miserably, known as CALM, on a campaign encouraging people to talk about mental health instead of suffering alone. He later worked with Talk Club and released a version of “Sweet Caroline” to raise money for men’s mental health.That is what makes Fury’s story different from a simple boxing comeback. His career already had the titles, big fights and packed stadiums. The more personal battle came when none of those things could make him feel better.Fury survived a difficult start to life, reached the top of boxing, lost his way and then found a route back. His story does not suggest that family support alone fixes depression or addiction. It shows something more practical: asking for help, accepting support and continuing the work can matter when someone is struggling.For Fury, the fight outside the ring became the one that changed how he viewed his life.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Week after losing coach, grieving Diya Chitale gets a moment to savour at Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For Diya Chitale, the last seven days have been an emotional roller coaster.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For Diya Chitale, the last seven days have been an emotional roller coaster. Exactly a week after losing Peter Engel, her coach since 2015, Diya stood on the Asian Games podium in Nagoya with the bronze medal around her neck, alongside Manush Shah. The duo had their moments against China’s top pairing of Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha before going down (0-4) 8-11, 5-11, 8-11, 2-11 in the mixed doubles semifinals at Sky Hall Toyota in Nagoya, settling for bronze. Despite the loss, Diya and Shah secured India’s first table-tennis medal of the ongoing Games.For Diya, Engel — who died on Sept 18 at 72 — was far more than a coach. “I had been working with Engel sir since 2015 and he is the person who completely developed my game. He was my go-to person for everything in TT,” she told TOI from Nagoya. Apart from the personal tragedy, there was also a lean spell for Diya and Shah to overcome. The world No. 8 mixed doubles pair had won two titles and finished runners-up once early in 2026, but their results dipped from June onwards. “I always believed that we are among the top few pairs and we can beat any pair on our day,” she said. Their belief was tested earlier on Friday.Drawn against Hong Kong’s world No. 4 Doo Hoi Kem and Wong Chun Ting, a pair they had lost to three times, the Indians knew execution had to be precise. They delivered, winning 3-1 (11-6, 13-15, 11-9, 11-5) to assure the nation its first TT medal of the Games before losing in semifinals. “We had played against them thrice and lost all our matches, but the last two matches were pretty close,” Diya said. “Hence we knew that if we had a clear strategy and if we could execute that well, we had a good chance. And we were able to do that today.”The medal carries weight far beyond the colour. It is India’s second Asian Games mixed doubles medal, after Sharath Kamal and Manika Batra’s bronze in Jakarta in 2018. “Winning a medal at the Games in our sport is huge and extra sweet since all the powerhouses in TT come from Asia — China, Japan, South Korea and so on,” she said. Diya dedicated her medal to Engel, paying her a personal tribute. “It would have been wonderful for him to see me achieve this today. This medal is for him.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
