articles.title: From 'it's all over' to Asian Games gold: Suruchi Inder Singh's stunning 48-hour turnaround
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: “Bas reset button dabaya maine,” Suruchi Inder Singh said after turning her disappointment into an Asian Games gold medal for India within two
articles.body: NEW DELHI: “Bas reset button dabaya maine,” Suruchi Inder Singh said after turning her disappointment into an Asian Games gold medal for India within two days. Suruchi and her teammate Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team event, finishing on top at the Aichi General Shooting Range on Friday.Suruchi, who was among the top medal contenders in the individual event, had endured a disappointing outing just two days earlier.The shooter, who won four individual World Cup gold medals in 2025 in Buenos Aires, Munich, Lima and Doha, including the World Cup Final, failed to qualify for the final of the individual 10m air pistol event.In a field of 55 shooters, she finished 26th in qualification with a score of 568-12x.The dejection was all over her face. She removed her shooting glasses, packed her pistol into its case, shook hands with her coach and support staff, and silently walked out of the Aichi General Shooting Gallery.Suruchi had dominated the event with her individual performances for almost two years and knew the expectations were high. But they all came crashing down in the space of an hour. Her silence said it all.Suruchi was shaken by the performance. But she knew she had another chance.On Friday, Suruchi returned, took aim and produced a stunning turnaround. She not only clinched gold for India but also paired with Kamaljeet to shoot a Games and Asian record of 484.6 and finish on top of the podium.Asked how the 20-year-old managed to turn things around within 48 hours, Suruchi said she had to hit the ‘reset button’. She spoke to her mother, met her coach and spent time reflecting on what had gone wrong.The message she kept telling herself was simple: “It’s okay, it’s done.”“I would say that perhaps it just wasn’t my day during the individual event. Or maybe I faced a technical problem that I couldn’t understand, which prevented me from recovering. I had to hit the reset button because I had another competition in two days. And I couldn’t do it alone. I spoke to my coach and my parents, and staying with them helped me get my mind in the right place,” Suruchi told TimesofIndia.com during a media interaction.“As soon as my match ended, I told myself, ‘It’s okay, it’s done.’ After that, my mother called and helped me get back into the right frame of mind. I had lunch and spent some time at the range. But by evening, I started feeling low again. I didn’t feel like eating anything after the disappointing match, nor did I feel like talking to anyone,” the pistol shooter said.“I felt that it was all over for me at the Games. There was no other match left for me. It felt like everything had come to an end. Once that one match was over, I felt there was nothing left,” she said.Kamaljeet gets a second chanceSuruchi was not the only one who had endured disappointment in the individual event. Kamaljeet too had a difficult outing in the men’s 10m air pistol event. He finished ninth in qualification on Thursday, missing out on the final by just one point.He feared his maiden Asian Games campaign would end without a medal.“I was very sad. I was depressed because I felt that I would have to leave my maiden Asian Games without a medal,” he said.But Kamaljeet was handed another opportunity when he was brought into the mixed team event in place of Kedarling Balakrishna Uchaganve.“Samresh sir told me there was a change in the 10m mixed team event and that I was being brought in place of Kedarling. I was overjoyed when I got the message. I had got one more chance to win the elusive Asian Games medal,” he said.Kamaljeet grabbed that opportunity with both hands, teaming up with Suruchi to produce a record-breaking performance.“I am always ready to shoot. I like such challenges every day,” Kamaljeet said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tarik Skubal fuels Dodgers’ playoff hopes with domination of Giants
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal saved his best for his last start of the regular season
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO –– In his final tune-up of the regular season, Tarik Skubal looked like a well-oiled machine.

After looking good, but not often great, in his first couple months with the Dodgers , the team's marquee trade deadline acquisition tapped back into his two-time Cy Young-winning form on Friday night, carving up the San Francisco Giants in a 2-0 win that could portend big things in the playoffs.

During his scoreless seven-inning start, Skubal struck out 10 batters and allowed just three hits. He didn't issue a walk. He hardly even looked stressed during an uber-efficient 75-pitch domination.

In his entire MLB career, the only time he posted a better stat line might have been in his lone complete-game shutout last year against the Cleveland Guardians .

The Dodgers, of course, didn't need proof of such excellence from Skubal.

When they acquired him from the Tigers two months ago, they knew they had landed the one player available at this year's deadline capable of significantly boosting their World Series odds.

He didn't record a scoreless outing until two weeks ago in Cincinnati , when he blanked the Reds over seven innings with nine strikeouts and only three hits allowed. And even then, he turned right back around and allowed four runs in five innings against the Giants his last time –– before spending a few days earlier this week away from the team on the bereavement list .

Friday's rematch at Oracle Park followed an entirely different script.

Skubal was handed a 2-0 lead in the second, after Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit a pair of home runs in a three-batter sequence ( for Pages, it was his first long ball since returning from a fractured hand last week).

And from there, the 29-year-old Northern California native never looked back, pounding the Giants with a steady diet of fastballs and changeups to finish the year with a 12-7 record and 2.72 ERA overall (including a 5-2 record and 2.61 ERA in 10 starts with the Dodgers, the last four of which were all winning decisions).

In the process, Skubal touched 100 mph with his heater for only the third time this year, while also getting 12 whiffs on 25 swings with the pitch. His changeup was equally effective, inducing a swing-and-miss seven of the 14 times the Giants offered at it.

The only caveat to his gem: The Giants are trotting out what is effectively a Triple-A lineup, as they limp to the end of a dismal 2026 season in which all of their big stars first struggled, then got hurt.

Still, there are worse ways to enter the playoffs than off the back of what was arguably his most complete start all season.

Friday, after all, was exactly what the Dodgers were envisioning when they traded for Skubal at the deadline.

They will be hoping it's the start of more things to come in October.

articles.title: Dodgers shut out Giants 2-0 as Skubal dominates and Hernández, Pages go deep
articles.summary: The Dodgers keep rolling toward postseason after silencing Giants in San Francisco
articles.body:
The Dodgers (98-62) shutout the Giants (65-95) Friday night in San Francisco behind a dominant Tarik Skubal and a pair of home runs from Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages .

Despite a Giants lineup more akin to a Triple-A squad, Skubal looked completely dominant and efficient against the San Francisco bats. Skubal struck out 10 over seven shutout innings, and he only made 75 pitches in his final tuneup before his first postseason start with the Dodgers.

Will Smith 's health and success is key to the Dodgers heading into the postseason. Smith came into the game hitting .400 with eight hits including three home runs in his last seven games. Smith continued his hot hitting and lined a single in the first inning to give the Dodgers two runners in scoring position with two outs against Yunior Marté .

While Smith and Pages continued to ramp up their offense with solid nights at the plate, Shohei Ohtani had a rough one. Ohtani went 0-for-4 with three strikeouts.

There were three outfield assists in the first three innings of the game. Both teams attempted to stretch singles into doubles but were shut down with laser throws from the outfield.

Pages showed off his arm in center field in the bottom of the first behind Skubal, throwing out Victor Bericoto at second. Bericoto must not have read the scouting report on Pages and his cannon in center.

Teoscar Hernández quickly crushed the first pitch he saw from Marte for a solo homer to left to put the Dodgers on the board.

Pages has been trying to get at-bats in after missing more than a month. He looked in midseason form when he launched a solo home run to make it 2-0 in favor of the Dodgers, his first round-tripper since coming off the injured list.

Both teams tried to stretch singles into doubles but got mowed down by the opposition at second base. Kiké Hernández was thrown out by Marcelo Mayer at second for the second outfield assist of the game.

Smith collected his second hit of the night, a two-out single in the bottom of the third. Smith also tried to leg out a double, but was once again blocked by Mayer. The Dodgers challenged the call on the field, but the trifecta of outfield assists stood intact.

There was no need to push Skubal any further without anything on the line for the Dodgers during this final weekend series. Roki Sasaki took over for Skubal out of the bullpen for the eighth inning and struck out two. Sasaki and his giant yellow glove will certainly be looked to out of relief during the NLDS.

America's Catcher, Smith, picked up his third hit of the night in the top of the ninth. Despite the late-inning base runners, the Dodgers couldn't add on to their lead.

Tanner Scott took the ball with a two-run lead in the bottom of the ninth and secured the 2-0 shutout win with two strikeouts to put a bow on it.

articles.title: Florida Places SEC Rival on High Alert With Marquee Visitor for Ole Miss Game
articles.summary: Florida football is hosting two big name recruits, with one who could ruffle the feathers of this SEC power. The post Florida Places SEC Rival on High Alert...
articles.body:
The Florida Gators are rolling immediately under new head coach Jon Sumrall. Saturday presents them with a huge opportunity to reintroduce themselves into the national stage by beating No. 4 Ole Miss. But stunning the Rebels and coach Pete Golding isn't the only news to monitor out in Gainesville.

Same with the influx of recruits who will head to "The Swamp."

But the biggest visitor officially places one of Florida's SEC rivals on high alert. As Florida aims to flip this blue chip recruit.

Good news for Rebel fans, it's not one of their 2027 verbal commits. But bad news for the nation's top-ranked team.

Texas Commit Visiting for Ole Miss at Florida

Rivals recruiting insider Chad Simmons revealed Friday the official biggest visitor ahead of the top 25 showdown.

"One of the biggest names expected in Gainesville is five-star Texas commit Easton Royal. The New Orleans Brother Martin playmaker remains one of Florida's biggest flip targets," Simmons wrote.

So Florida continues to remain in hot pursuit of Royal. Sumrall clearly is using his past Louisiana connections, as he previously coached in Royal's hometown at Tulane.

The Gators aren't the only ones all over Royal in the attempt to swoop him up from the grasp of Steve Sarkisian and the Longhorns.

"LSU is heavily involved as well, but the Gators get another significant opportunity this weekend," Simmons said.

Landing Easton Royal will Shake Recruiting Landscape

And in the process, signal Florida's desire to reclaim its status as a top-ranked recruiting class.

Florida's recruiting efforts have taken a big hit post Urban Meyer. Previous coaches Will Muschamp, Dan Mullen and more recently Billy Napier delivered multiple recruiting misses. The latter coach ended up having a hard time keeping prominent commits from drifting off.

Sumrall clearly wants to change that narrative. His 2027 class ranks No. 8 overall, which places the Gators two spots behind Texas.

Florida catapults Texas if it lures in Royal to boost its offense moving forward. Royal possesses the run-after-catch element that can turn any offense into a deadly one. He's grabbed handoffs too out of the backfield, giving defenses fits there. So Florida nabs a potential Percy Harvin-type here for Sumrall's future Gator teams.

And Royal's not the only one to closely monitor.

Sumrall and the No. 21 Gators are all over a West Virginia pledge too, per Simmons.

"Royal won't be the only committed receiver worth watching. West Virginia commit Jacobi Pasley, out of Hinesville (Ga.) Bradwell Institute is also expected," Simmons wrote, adding its an official visit for Pasley.

So Florida can flip two wideouts on the same weekend. Which rises as the most aggressive recruiting weekend for Sumrall and this staff.

Those wideouts should fawn over Florida's multiple spread, Air Raid and pro style approach. But beating Ole Miss can pique their interest too. It'll fire off the signal that the Gators are back. And adding Royal plus Pasley sparks future national title chatter.

Ole Miss enters on upset alert, while Texas is on high alert recruiting wise.

articles.title: Indiana Survives Northwestern Rally in Big Ten Opener
articles.summary: Indiana opened Big Ten play with a hard-fought 29-23 victory over Northwestern on Friday night, surviving a furious fourth-quarter comeback attempt from the...
articles.body:
Indiana opened Big Ten play with a hard-fought 29-23 victory over Northwestern on Friday night, surviving a furious fourth-quarter comeback attempt from the Wildcats.

The No. 5 Hoosiers controlled much of the game early and built a 15-0 halftime lead. However, Northwestern refused to go away, turning the game into a tense finish before Indiana finally secured the victory.

Indiana's defense set the tone early, keeping Northwestern off the scoreboard throughout the first half.

The Hoosiers took a 2-0 lead in the opening quarter before adding 10 points in the second to take a 12-point advantage into halftime. Indiana added another field goal in the third quarter, extending its lead to 15-7 heading into the final period.

Northwestern had entered the game averaging 37.5 points per game and had scored 41 points against Colorado in its previous outing, but Indiana's defense managed to slow down the Wildcats for much of the night.

The Wildcats came alive in the fourth quarter.

Northwestern scored 16 points in the final period and continued to put pressure on Indiana as the Hoosiers tried to protect their lead. Indiana answered with 14 fourth-quarter points of its own, but the game remained a one-possession battle late.

The Wildcats had one final opportunity to make something happen, including a dramatic onside-kick attempt that nearly gave them another possession. Indiana ultimately recovered and was able to finish off the victory.

With the 29-23 win, Indiana improves to 4-0 and begins its Big Ten schedule with a victory.

The Hoosiers entered the night after dominating their first three games, outscoring their opponents 145-16. Friday night was a much different challenge, as Northwestern pushed Indiana throughout the second half and showed why it entered the matchup undefeated.

For Indiana, it wasn't the comfortable victory many expected after its dominant nonconference start. Instead, the Hoosiers had to withstand a late Northwestern charge and make the plays necessary to preserve the win.

Indiana now turns its attention toward the rest of a challenging Big Ten schedule, while Northwestern leaves Bloomington knowing it pushed one of the nation's top ranked teams to the final minutes.

The Hoosiers survived and that's all that matters in Big Ten play.

articles.title: Padres can’t clinch home field as desperate Diamondbacks keep hopes alive
articles.summary: With thoughts of locking up home field for the NL Wild Card Series on their minds, the San Diego Padres instead felt firsthand the desperation of the Arizona...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO – With thoughts of locking up home field for the NL Wild Card Series on their minds, the San Diego Padres instead felt firsthand the desperation of the Arizona Diamondbacks in a 11-4 loss on Friday night at Petco Park.

Casey Mize allowed three homers in his four innings for the Padres (89-71), who had early basepath traffic cut down by double plays in three of the first four innings. Six different players had RBI for Arizona (86-74), led by four from Geraldo Perdomo , as they kept their playoff hopes alive with their eighth road win in their past nine.

The capacity crowd at Petco Park gave the Padres a standing ovation as they took the field, the large video board in left field emblazoned with a graphic celebrating the club's clinching of its fifth playoff spot in the last seven seasons.

But the wind was immediately taken out of the sails, as trade deadline acquisition Lars Nootbaar got into an elevated sinker from Mize, launching the first pitch to right center field for his eighth home run of the season. It marked the 11th game in a row the D-Backs have hit a long ball.

That wasn't all, as Gabriel Moreno singled with one out and Perdomo followed up by roping a triple down the right field line that Dustin Harris couldn't play cleanly off the base of the angled wall. It brought in the second run of the inning, then Corbin Carroll followed up with a RBI sacrifice fly, making it five games in a row where Arizona has scored in the opening inning — they put up multiple in all three of their wins at Colorado .

After the Padres came up empty despite getting consecutive singles in the home half of the first, Arizona added on in the second as Jordan Lawlar homered on an 0-1 count. His sixth depth charge of the season landed on the Petco Porch, just 334 feet from home.

But San Diego was able to get back a pair their next time up, as Jackson Merrill and Xander Bogaerts opened up with consecutive singles. Luis Campusano netted an RBI on a ground-out to second, then Jake Cronenworth followed up by knocking in Bogaerts with an RBI single up the middle. A double-play lineout ended the inning.

But Mize walked Perdomo with one down, and then after a pop out he left slider center-cut for Nolan Arenado , who bashed it into the second level of the Western Metal Supply Co. building for a pair of RBI and his 30th homer of the year.

Arizona added another in the fourth as Nootbaar drew a one-out walk and advanced to second on a ground-out. Moreno followed up by punching an RBI single through the right side to push the lead beyond grand slam range.

That would be Mize's final inning, as he finished with four innings pitched and the seven runs allowed on seven hits — three which went for home runs, matching the most he's allowed this season. He also walked two versus just a lone strikeout.

David Morgan took the fifth and worked around a walk, then Kyle Hart got the sixth. After getting the first two outs quickly, Hart walked three in a row and Perdomo made it hurt, hitting a bases-clearing double to center that Merrill was unable to field.

Arizona added another in the seventh against Jason Adam , who loaded the bases with two walks and a hit by pitch before getting a double play ball and a fly-out. Cronenworth added an RBI in the seventh, hustling to beat out a potential double-play ball after singles by Sung-Mun Song and one stung off the left field wall by Campusano.

Wandy Peralta pitched the eighth, getting the D-backs in order thanks to Jase Bowen robbing Perdomo of a home run in straight-away center field. It happened again in the ninth, with Bowen ranging over to left-center and leaping to take a homer away from Tim Tawa .

The Padres were able to tack another run on in the eighth, as Harris walked with one out and then Ty France did with two gone, ending Pfaadt 's night. Reliever Ryne Nelson allowed an RBI single to Song

Brandon Pfaadt earned his eighth win for Arizona, going 7 2/3 innings and allowing four runs on nine hits, with seven strikeouts and two walks. He won both of his games at Petco Park.

With the Chicago Cubs dropping both games of their double-header today at Boston , as well as the Philadelphia Phillies loss at home to Tampa Bay, the Padres remain just one win away from clinching home field for the NL Wild Card Series. They can also clinch if Chicago and Philadelphia each lose one more game.

Arizona is now just a game back of the final NL Wild Card.

The Padres have named Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56 ERA) as their starter for the Saturday game against the Diamondbacks, while Arizona has not named a starter for the game. First pitch is scheduled for 5:40 p.m. at Petco Park.

articles.title: The 10 biggest Cincinnati sports letdowns since 2000. Do you agree?
articles.summary: Life as a Cincinnati sports fan isn't always easy. Here are the top 10 biggest letdowns since 2000.
articles.body:
Life as a Cincinnati sports fan isn't always easy.

The Bengals have yet to win a Super Bowl. The Reds haven't won a playoff series since 1995. The Cincinnati Bearcats last won a national title in basketball in 1962, and Xavier has never made it past the Elite Eight.

Top 10 Cincinnati sports letdowns of the 21st century (ranked!)

So, what are some of the bigger heartbreaks since 2000? There have been plenty, and Enquirer sports columnist Jason Williams put the top 10 in a ranked list.

See his rankings in the gallery above and watch a condensed video of me breaking down his choices in the video at the top of the page.

You can watch my FULL video explaining it all in the YouTube video below .

images.caption: We compiled a list of the top 10 Cincinnati sports letdowns since Y2K . Reds. Bengals. Bearcats. Musketeers. They've all inflicted serious pain on their fans. But what's the one moment we just still can't get over? Count down with us as the groans grow louder with each pick. (Sam Greene)

The fire sale that saw the departure of Sonny Gray, Nick Castellanos, Eugenio Suarez, Jesse Winker and others. The "sell the team, Bob" movement on social media. Phil Castellini's "where you gonna go?" comment on Opening Day. And 100 losses. Yep, perhaps the most forgettable calendar year in Reds history. (Kareem Elgazzar/The Enquirer)
No. 9: UC, Xavier flop as high seeds in 2018 NCAA Tournament. (Kareem Elgazzar/The Enquirer)

Xavier was the No. 1 seed in the West. UC received a No. 2 seed in the South. Could half of the Final Four be Queen City teams? Those dreams didn't last past the first weekend of the tourney – and they died hard. UC blew a 22-point lead with 11 minutes remaining in a second-round loss to Nevada. Xavier squandered a 12-point lead with less than 11 minutes left vs. Florida State. It all happened in a matter of hours on March 18, 2018. And college basketball in Cincinnati hasn’t recovered. Brutal. (Sam Greene)
No. 8: Joe Burrow's 2023 wrist injury. (Cara Owsley/The Enquirer)

The big letdown here: Burrow's season-ending wrist injury in Baltimore caused reality to set in that the franchise quarterback is injury-prone and Cincinnati may never win a Super Bowl during his time. Burrow missed most of training camp with a calf injury. He was just heating up when the Bengals went to Baltimore in mid-November, having thrown for more than 340 yards in the previous two games and helping Cincinnati take a 5-4 record into the game. The Bengals went on to miss the playoffs and haven't been back since the 2022 season. (Cara Owsley/The Enquirer)
No. 7: The Bengals' 2021 Super Bowl loss. (Albert Cesare/The Enquirer)
No. 6: Penalty costs Bengals 2022 AFC Championship game (Jan. 2023). (Kareem Elgazzar/The Enquirer)

articles.body: Defending champions Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty suffered a major setback at the Asian Games, crashing out in the first round after losing to Thailand’s Pakkapon Teeraratsakul and Peeratchai Sukphun on Friday.The Indian pair started strongly, winning the opening game 21-12, but failed to maintain their momentum. The world No. 36 Thai duo fought back to win the next two games 21-19, 21-14 in 64 minutes.Satwik and Chirag looked set for a routine victory after dominating the first game, but the Thais made the most of the Indians’ errors in the second. The Indians saved one, but Pakkapon produced a superb cross-court winner to level the match.The deciding game turned one-sided as Satwik and Chirag appeared increasingly fatigued. Their returns lacked their usual power, forcing the world’s best attacking pair into an unfamiliar defensive role as the Thais repeatedly unleashed smashes.The defeat came after a demanding schedule and limited recovery time. Satwik said the team had returned late from the previous night’s event.“Quite patchy... We know these situations will happen. It will get tense because it will be tricky playing continuously in the team event. We were here till 12 last night,” Satwik told reporters.He also admitted that the pair needed to improve their mental approach.“It’s the mental part. articles.title: Christian Brothers Academy blasts Shenendehowa in Class AA football
articles.summary: CBA, ranked No. 4 in the state, rolled up 324 yards in the first half
articles.body:
CLIFTON PARK - George Karame is one of the area's best football players, but his role as a two-way starting lineman for the Christian Brothers Academy does not afford the senior many chances to step into the limelight. Friday night, Karame reached the end zone.

Karame, a nimble 6-foot-1, 285-pound defensive tackle, managed to snare an interception in the end zone during the second quarter as the Brothers were scoring at will in their Class AA contest against Shenendehowa. Late in the second quarter, Shen senior quarterback Jack Clawson attempted to avoid a sack in the end zone and heaved the ball a few yards forward into the awaiting hands of Karame.

"My friend Myles (Johnson, CBA's senior linebacker) almost had the tackle (for a) safety," Karame said. "He threw the ball and I caught it. The greatest feeling in my life."

"I love that," CBA senior running back/linebacker Tommy Toher said. "He's my guy. He is doing the dirty work and getting the shine."

CBA left the Mustangs in the dark, scoring 54 points during the first half and cruising to a 61-14 victory. The Brothers (4-0 overall, 3-0 Class AA) surpassed the 60-point plateau for the third time this season.

"The lines dominated and we made some insane plays. Coach (Jim Canfield, who coaches the offensive and defensive lines) is the best line coach in Section 2," Karame said. "This was just awesome."

Karame has added starting offensive line duties this season and he made his presence felt Friday.

"I am telling him he was to play both ways the entire game, but if we can continue do this in the first half of games he won't have to," CBA coach Bobby Burns. "We were focused, the kids practiced hard all week and we came up some big plays. They had a couple of big plays, but we did what we wanted to do."

CBA led 27-0 before Shen responded with a 69-yard pass play from Clawson to Elijah Woodrow. The visitors extended the advantage to 54-7 at halftime.

The only close game this season for the Brothers was a 21-14 triumph over Saratoga Springs in Week 2, a contest that has served as motivation.

"That game gave us a chance to see what we needed to work on and improve on," Karame said. "We know we can score 60 points on any team in the section."

"That is going to drive us every week," Toher said. "Saratoga played a good game. Using that game has helped us. We put up 60 points coming here. It means a lot to our guys. That was impressive, but it is what we should. If we prepare well and put in that type of effort each week, we can do this each. We are building to where we want to be. This is just another confidence. We are staying humble and moving on the next one."

Toher opened the scoring with a 19-yard touchdown run. Shen's first series on offense stalled and CBA senior Michael Berben blocked a punt that Alex Rivera scored on to make it 13-0.

"We did anything we wanted to do in this game," Burns said. "Defensively, we're pretty good. They couldn't run the ball and we had those two punt blocks. … If we play the way we are capable, prep well and play well on Friday nights, we can do special things."

Toher finished the game with nine carries for 90 yards and two touchdowns in a contest filled with standouts for CBA.

"This game was impressive. We did all the things we came here to do tonight," Toher said.

articles.title: Warriors dominate Berne Union in MSL-Cardinal clash
articles.summary: Worthington Christian rushed for 280 yards and scored 42 unanswered points to defeat Berne Union 56 17 on Friday.
articles.body:
Amanda-Clearcreek football hosts Licking Valley

SUGAR GROVE — Worthington Christian ran for 280 yards on 37 carries and scored 42 unanswered points as the Warriors ran away with Berne Union for a 56-17 victory Friday night, Sept. 25.

"They are very physical up front, and they obviously had (defensive) pressure on us all night," Berne Union coach Tony Hurps said. "So, it was pretty tough for us to run the ball or do much all night."

Worthington Christian (4-2) received the opening kickoff and drove down the field with relative ease, going 65 yards in 10 plays that ended with a nine-yard touchdown run from Josh Unger to put the Warriors on top 7-0 just four minutes in.

After Berne Union (3-3) went three-and-out on its first possession, Worthington Christian again moved the ball quickly into Rocket territory. On second down at the Rockets 44-yard line, the Warriors attempted a wide receiver bubble screen to the left. However, Berne Union's Jackson Little read the play perfectly and jumped the route to intercept the pass from Warriors quarterback Isaac Zerkle, and Little ran the ball 56 yards for a touchdown to tie the game at 7-7.

"We were trying to mix and match and disguise coverage as best we could," Hurps said, "and that was one that we guessed right on."

The Warriors responded with a six-play, 55-yard drive that saw Unger score his second touchdown of the night to put the visitors back in the lead. And on the ensuing kickoff, Berne Union's James Hocking returned the kick 66 yards down to the Warriors' 26-yard line, setting up his team in great position.

The Rockets did not waste that opportunity. On the first play, quarterback Carson Kiger took the snap and rolled to his left to evade pressure and spun a perfect spiral pass to Hocking for the touchdown to tie the game at 14-14.

Berne Union's defense then responded with a big play when Cameron Brown and Dilan Carter combined on a tackle and popped the ball free, and Aiden Long recovered. It set the Rockets up on their own 40 with a drive to try and take the lead. However, the Warrior defense forced a three-and-out, and the Rockets punted away; Dom Ortega returned the ball inside the five-yard line.

Two plays later, Bailey Murray dove into the end zone from two yards out to give the Warriors a 21-14 lead with nine minutes left in the first half.

Later in the quarter with Rockets down 28-14, Hurps threw a new offensive wrinkle into play with senior receiver James Hocking in the backfield as a running back in an old-school I formation. Hocking's first carry was a 28-yard gain, and after a few more plays the Rockets were inside the 10 yard line.

But after getting stuffed on runs up the middle by the physical Warrior defensive line, the Rockets went for it on fourth down from the three and came up short. Kiger dropped back to pass and rolled to his left, looking for an open receiver, and ultimately tried to evade some defenders and run it in, but was tackled for a loss and the Rockets turned the ball over on downs with just two minutes left to play in the first half.

"We just couldn't capitalize on it and I think that hurt us going into halftime," Hurps said of the sequence.

Berne Union's only other score of the night came on a 34-yard field goal that Aidan Harris boomed through the uprights with 5:48 left in the game.

Hocking was the leading rusher for the Rockets with 35 yards on five carries, while Kiger finished with 63 passing yards while completing 9 of 21 passes. As a team, Berne Union managed just 73 rushing yards on 27 attempts, good for a 2.7 yard per-carry average.

Unger led Worthington Christian with 87 rushing yards on 13 attempts and three touchdowns, while Dom Ortega, Bailey Murray, TiJe Adediran all had a rushing touchdown and Zerkle added one passing touchdown.

Berne Union will aim to rebound with league play next week as it travels to Grove City Christian.

"We touched on it in the huddle: ' This game hurts.' That's a really good team, and all of our losses have been to pretty good teams," Hurps said. "But we don't have any league losses. (Grove City Christian) Next week, they played Worthing Christian, so we have a common opponent, and they didn't score, so I think that's going to be a really tough matchup. I think we're two of the better teams in the league, so that's still out in front for those guys."

articles.title: Brainerd scores 21 consecutive as Sartell drops to 1-3 on the season
articles.summary: With 5:53 left in the third quarter, Sartell took a commanding 28-14 lead. Then Brainerd quarterback Malik Lauer took over.
articles.body:
SARTELL, Minn. — With 5:53 left in the third quarter, junior quarterback Daylon Holter muscled his way into the endzone from a few yards out to give the Sabres a commanding two-score lead over Brainerd, capping off a six-minute and seven second drive to start the second half.

The Sartell defense forced a Warrior punt to give the ball right back to Holter and the offense with a chance to all but seal the win to go up 21 points heading into the fourth quarter, but the Sabres would relinquish the opportunity and punt it right back to sophomore quarterback Malik Lauer and the Brainerd offense.

Not that there was any debate to be had, but that would end up being a poor decision.

Lauer connected with Luke Merseth from 40 yards out to set up a Kyle Syrdal score, then he took it himself from 34 yards a few minutes later. Now tied at 28, Lauer called his own number one more time and found paydirt again, this time from 14 yards for the go-ahead score with 2:35 left in the game. Twenty-one unanswered points orchestrated by a 5-foot-10 sophomore to drop Sartell's record to 1-3 on the season and seal a 35-28 victory for Brainerd in a competitive Central Lakes showdown.

"I just trusted my team," Lauer said. "I haven't been able to run like that all season. It was amazing. I felt like I was playing eighth grade football again, just running all the time. Our defense just needed momentum, but once they got the stop and we scored, they knew what they had to do and converted."

The sophomore gunslinger totaled 94 rushing yards and two touchdowns to pair with 161 yards and two touchdowns through the air.

The loss marks the third time this season that Sartell has lost by single digit points.

"I'm proud of how our kids played, but we made some mistakes in all phases of the game," Sartell coach Scott Henges said. "Brainerd's a talented-enough team that when you do that and give them chances, they have a chance to convert. We'll watch the tape, see what things we can fix and [then] fix them. It's just a matter of getting some conversions and first downs or stopping a team on third down or fourth down; we can do that."

Despite the mistakes, the Sabres were able to establish the run game for the third week in a row as senior running back Jonah Ambrosier put up 200 yards and two touchdowns for the third week in a row.

Of course, the gaudy numbers do not mean much without the record to back it up.

Henges knows his team will not tuck its tail as it approaches the midway point of the season.

"I have spent all year with these guys," Henges said. "We have good leadership; the guys aren't going to quit. They're frustrated, as am I, but they'll be back and they'll be ready to go. That is the expectation, it's nothing I have to tell them. They do it, so I don't have any question about that."

The Sabres host St. Francis (1-3) on Oct. 2 for their homecoming game. Brainerd hosts Bemidji (0-4) the same day.

articles.title: Arenado, Perdomo lead Diamondbacks over Padres 11-4 to stay alive in wild-card hunt
articles.summary: Nolan Arenado hit one of Arizona's three home runs and Geraldo Perdomo drove in four runs for the Diamondbacks, who beat San Diego 11-4 on Friday night to re...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Nolan Arenado hit one of Arizona 's three home runs and Geraldo Perdomo drove in four runs for the Diamondbacks , who beat San Diego 11-4 on Friday night to remain alive for the National League's final wild-card spot.

Lars Nootbar and Jordan Lawlar also homered in the victory, which kept San Diego from clinching the No. 4 seed and home-field advantage in the wild-card round next week.

Brandon Pfaadt (8-3) beat the Padres for the third time this season with 7 2/3 innings. He allowed four runs and nine hits, struck out seven and walked two.

San Diego and Chicago clinched wild-card berths on Thursday, leaving Philadelphia and Arizona to fight it out for the third spot. Arizona is one game behind the Phillies with two to play.

The Diamondbacks and Padres knew that the Cubs had been swept by Boston in a doubleheader and that Philadelphia had lost to Tampa Bay.

The Padres then just needed to beat the Diamondbacks to clinch the No. 4 seed.

But Casey Mize (6-10) allowed the three home runs to jeopardize his spot on the wild-card roster and the Padres were booed a few times a night after clinching their club-record third straight postseason berth with a 4-2 win at the Los Angeles Dodgers .

Nootbar drove Mize's first pitch into the home-run porch in the right-field corner. Perdomo hit an RBI triple and Corbin Carroll a sacrifice fly to make it 3-0.

Lawlar homered to right field with one out in the second. Arenado drove a two-run shot off the third level of the Western Metal Supply Co. brick warehouse in the left-field corner with two outs in the third, his 30th, for a 6-2 lead.

Gabriel Moreno hit an RBI single in the fourth and, after Kyle Hart walked the bases loaded in the sixth, Perdomo cleared them with a double that bounced off the glove of retreating center fielder Jackson Merrill and then off the padded fence.

Padres center fielder Jase Bowen robbed Perdomo of a home run to end the eighth and then stole one from Tim Tawa to end the ninth.

Arizona was pondering its options for Saturday night after placing RHP Corbin Burnes on the injured list with shoulder inflammation. The Padres will go with RHP Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56 ERA).

articles.title: Lee Beebe Jr.'s career-best rushing game saves Indiana in close call against Northwestern
articles.summary: Lee Beebe Jr. ran for a career-high 203 yards and a touchdown as Indiana held off Northwestern 29-23 on Friday night to extend its win streak to 20 games.
articles.body:
Lee Beebe Jr. looked like Indiana 's Heisman contender on Friday night.

The fifth-year back more than supported quarterback Josh Hoover , rushing for a career-high 203 yards and a touchdown as Indiana held off Northwestern 29-23 on Friday night to extend its win streak to 20 games.

Beebe ran for 144 yards in the fourth quarter, including a 70-yard burst and a four-yard touchdown run for the defending national champions. He successfully filled in for starting running back Turbo Richard , who was injured in the first half.

Beebe's previous career rushing high was 161 yards back in 2024, when he played for UAB. He gained nearly 1,500 yards from scrimmage in two-plus seasons with the Blazers, then joined the Hoosiers last season.

He started off hot for Indiana last year before suffering a torn right ACL against Indiana State on Sept. 12 that cost him the rest of the season.

He's back this season and was ready to be the workhorse late against Northwestern. He carried 12 times in the fourth quarter and clinched the game with a tackle-breaking four-yard run on a third-and-1 in the final minute.

Hoover completed 19 of 29 passes for 201 yards and a touchdown. It was the first Big Ten win for the TCU transfer.

articles.title: Kurt Warner fires back after Jayden Daniels injury comments spark backlash
articles.summary: Kurt Warner has pushed back on criticism surrounding his comments about Jayden Daniels potentially playing through his latest elbow injury after comparing it...
articles.body:
Kurt Warner has pushed back on criticism surrounding his comments about Jayden Daniels potentially playing through his latest elbow injury after comparing it to an injury he suffered during his own NFL career.

The Hall of Fame quarterback explained that he was not telling Daniels he should play through the injury or questioning his toughness.

Warner's comments came after Daniels re-dislocated his left elbow during Washington's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Commanders later confirmed that Daniels would not undergo surgery or be placed on injured reserve, although there is currently no official timetable for his return.

Kurt Warner clarifies his comments after Jayden Daniels injury comparison

Warner originally discussed his experience on NFL Live, recalling how he dislocated his left elbow while playing for the Arizona Cardinals in 2007 before returning the following week with a brace.

Because Daniels' injury is also to his non-throwing arm, Warner suggested there could potentially be a path for the Commanders quarterback to return in a similar situation.

That comparison quickly drew criticism, prompting Warner to address the reaction on Instagram.

"I'm not telling anybody, 'Hey, you need to go out and play. You're not tough if you don't go out and play. That's not what I said at all. Those weren't the words that I used, so don't try to put those words into my mouth," Warner said.

He later acknowledged that his own injury was not identical to Daniels' situation.

"No, my situation is not Jaden Daniels' exact situation. He's a younger guy; he's a more mobile guy. There's lots of things to consider," Warner said.

Warner explained that his intention was to give viewers perspective based on an injury he had personally experienced, while recognising that Daniels' circumstances are different.

Meanwhile, Washington has taken a cautious approach. Daniels underwent evaluations with multiple specialists and will remain on the 53-man roster, with the Commanders describing him as week-to-week.

Marcus Mariota will start against the Seattle Seahawks while Daniels works towards a return, with teammates rallying around both quarterbacks.

Dan Quinn said the team would wait for all the available medical information before making further decisions, leaving Daniels' return timeline open as Washington prepares for a crucial stretch of games.

articles.title: West Allegheny football grinds out rivalry win over Moon Area
articles.summary: After a one-point loss to Montour in Week 4, West Allegheny High School football grinded out a rivalry win over Moon Area.
articles.body:
There could have been nerves along the West Allegheny sidelines late in the game despite a 21-13 lead as Moon completed five straight passes to get inside the Indians' 20-yard line.

Just last week, West Allegheny dropped a 1-point decision to Montour.

"I wasn't nervous, but I was a little anxious," said West Allegheny coach Bob Palko, in his second stint as head coach after winning state titles the first time around.

"We need to get these guys to understand what it takes to win."

Beaver Valley Week 5 high school football top frames

The team understood this game as they forced a fumble, Austin Probert recovered, and West Allegheny ran out the clock for the win.

Palko's post-game instructions to his team was all about those lessons learned and he continued to teach.

"We're always teaching, we can't waste these moments," Palko said. "We have gold nuggets here that we have to develop."

Palko's lessons are not falling on deaf ears, either as the team continues to grow in preparation for conference play next week.

"It feels amazing to win this game," said senior Brodie Cornell, who scored the final two touchdowns, gaining 59 yards rushing, 57 receiving, and added a 43-yard punt return. His dad, Bryan, has been on the West Allegheny staff since Palko's first term.

"There are always butterflies before every game but coach had us ready," Cornell said. "I grew up around Coach Palko, he was like a second dad to me. To play three years and then get a chance to play for him is great."

It isn't only the seniors that are taking advantage of the opportunity. Junior Nico Police scored the Indians' first touchdown on a 15-yard run and intercepted a pass to set up the second.

"This is an unbelievable feeling and we just want to soak up every minute," Police said. "On the interception, we were playing quarters and reading the quarterback's eyes. We knew they'd be throwing a lot."

Moon did, indeed, throw a lot. Junior Cristiano Kinol threw 40 times, completing 22 for 281 yards. Senior Savario Vandetti caught eight of those passes for 157 yards and scored the first touchdown on a 38-yard punt return.

Despite those numbers, though, Kinol wasn't the only outstanding quarterback on the field. Senior Mason Bryan rushed 24 times for 120 yards and passed for 73 yards and two touchdowns. His fakes were good enough that he was usually tackled even when he handed the ball off, too.

"When I first started as quarterback when I was a kid," Bryan said with a smile. "I thought the quarterback was the one who didn't get hit.

"But it's always great to beat Moon — we grew up with most of those kids; I wish they were in our section, but it's still good to get a win."

As he watched the interview, Palko interjected, "That's one gritty kid."

It seems, in fact, that Palko is intent on developing a whole lot of gritty kids.

articles.body:
Scotland travel to Ljubljana on Saturday to open their UEFA Nations League B campaign against Slovenia at Stadion Stožice.

The visitors arrive in uncertain form after a difficult run of results that ended with Steve Clarke leaving his position as manager. During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Scotland recovered from early friendly defeats by securing a narrow 1-0 victory over Haiti . However, they later suffered a 1-0 loss to Morocco and a 3-0 defeat against Brazil , results that confirmed their elimination in the group stage. Under new head coach Sébastien Pocognoli , Scotland will be looking to end a two-match losing run while also improving a defence that has conceded too many goals.

The match marks the beginning of a new chapter for Scotland, although Pocognoli's first assignment has been made more difficult by several important absences.

Experienced midfielder Kenny McLean and veteran left-back Kieran Tierney both withdrew from the squad earlier this week because of fitness concerns.

Scotland are also missing attacking options Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland , leaving the new manager with limited choices in the final third.

Pocognoli has responded by making major changes to the squad and bringing eight uncapped players into the senior group.

Blackburn Rovers midfielder Kristi Montgomery, aged 22, was called up as a late replacement for McLean. His inclusion adds another inexperienced option to a squad undergoing significant change ahead of the Nations League campaign.

In attack, the recalled Oli McBurnie is expected to be considered for a starting role. He could lead the line alone or form a partnership with Robbie Ure or Lewis Ferguson as Pocognoli attempts to build a new-look Scotland forward line.

The manager will hope his reshaped team can produce a positive result in his first match in charge.

articles.title: Logan-Rogersville's Joe Roche called one of the best running backs in Missouri
articles.summary: Logan-Rogersville is off to its best start since 2011. Joe Roche led the team with four touchdowns against Bolivar on Friday.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD — Joe Roche broke tackle after tackle on Friday, Sept. 25. The senior running back was unstoppable in Logan-Rogersville's 42-13 win over Bolivar.

"I'm glad he's on our team. I love Joe," Rogersville head coach Joel Wells said. "I think he's one of the best backs in the state. I really do. He's a college football player."

Roche scored four touchdowns in the win, all of them coming in the first half. The secret to the running back's ability to break tackles was revealed after the game with a smile.

"I think it's because I sweat so much, they just slip off me," Roche laughed. "I really don't know, I'm just running and if a dude comes, I'm going to try and swing and get him off me any way that I can."

Logan-Rogersville takes down Bolivar football in Week 5

The senior put together 218 yards on 30 carries. Roche's performance helped Rogersville (5-0) snag another big win.

This is the Wildcats' best start to a season since 2011, when they started 6-0 and later won the Class 3 state title over John Burroughs.

"I'm extremely proud of what our team has been able to do," Wells said. "We are not done yet."

Bolivar actually started the scoring via a Chapel Banner passing touchdown to Paden Yates on the opening drive of the game. Then Roche went to work scoring two touchdowns from short yardage and a 10-yard burst.

Before halftime, Roche exploded for a 47-yard touchdown down the far sideline.

"I saw the hole and I saw Sky was back there blocking his guy well for me and I went off him," Roche said. "That dude pursued me so hard, I'm surprised that I even got that. I tried everything to outrun him."

In the second half, quarterback Kasimir Manczuk scored two rushing touchdowns to add to the Wildcats' lead.

The third quarter featured five turnovers between the two teams. Rogersville's Lucas White staged two interceptions to highlight the defense in the win.

"Huge moment," Wells said. "We knew he was going to have a big year this year. We are extremely proud of him coming up with some big plays here."

On paper, Rogersville has looked flawless. They've won each game by at least 16 points. The offense has scored more than 35 points in each game, while the defense has surrendered no more than 19 points.

Wells believes the best is still ahead for his team. The Wildcats continue to climb the Class 4 ranking, currently sitting at No. 3. Only No. 1 Kearney (5-0) and No. 2 Savannah (5-0) are ahead of the Wildcats.

"We haven't played our best football yet," Wells said. "We have a lot to improve on, but I love our team and I'm just fortunate to be their head coach."

Rogersville will face Hillcrest (1-2) on the road next week.

articles.title: No. 1 Bloomington South football survives gut check vs. Columbus North
articles.summary: Panthers need a big second half to rally past stubborn Bull Dogs' defense. Here's how they did it.
articles.body:
Bloomington South visits Martinsville in football action | Our best photos

BLOOMINGTON — Columbus North's football team came in zigging when the scouting report said the Bull Dogs should be zagging.

Different looks. Milking the clock on every snap to shorten the game. Avoiding tendencies. Stunting South's zone-read running game. They made Class 5A No. 1 Bloomington South sweat in the second half for the first time this season before the Panthers were able to pull out a 24-7 win on a perfect Friday night at Huff Memorial Field.

After falling behind for the first time all season, 7-0, South had to settle for field goal, then quickly got the ball again at the Columbus North 48. Duncan Combs zipped a screen pass to Jonathan Winstead on the home sideline with two Bull Dogs in front of him. Connor Parker shoved one to the side and Winstead darted by the other, galloping all the way to the end zone.

"That was a great momentum swing," Combs said. "Coming out of half, we had the missed kickoff return, but to get on offense and in one play and score a touchdown, that's great momentum. Jonny's super fast. Once he caught it and I saw Connor push his guy to the sideline, I knew he'd score."

Those 10 points in 1:52 propelled the Panthers to 24 unanswered points. Combs was 9-of-11 for 159 yards and three touchdowns in the second half after a less than stellar start.

It was 0-0 at halftime, but the break was more teaching than yelling.

"We kind of got in there and obviously, we're disappointed with ourselves offensively," Combs said. "We didn't play great, but they came out with different stuff that we haven't seen on film. So we had to go in, fix the gameplan, correct it to where we could attack the holes and it worked."

Columbus North keeps Panthers on their toes

The Bull Dogs tossed in some new looks and tried to shorten the game to keep South's potent offense off the field. It worked for 30 minutes.

"Some different approaches for us," South coach Gabe Johnson said. "We expect that. That's the hard part I think sometimes teams go into playing us and think, 'Let's change things up.' In football, you look at tendencies and that more you can change that up, you can catch people off-guard."

It was the start of a tough four-game finish for South and the first true test of the season.

"I thought our defense played really well," Johnson said. "Our offense was off-key, and they eventually got it going. I am 100% OK with a game like that. I told our kids, we can't go into every game thinking it's going to be 35-0 at halftime and that won't be the case moving forward."

The first half was a slog for South, which ran 15 times for just 41 yards and got 76 yards in the air. South owned great field position, as the punt and kickoffs pinned CN back. But they missed a field goal and had an interception in the end zone.

"They lined up in what we call and Eagle defense that just gives you problems," Johnson said. "They were trying to take away inside-zone, which is what we do. And we were not great up front. We've got things we've got to do to improve.

"We've got to run the ball better. Their plan was to get us in third-and-long and they did that. We didn't handle it well sometimes."

Still, the real key to it all was South's defense, which made sure it was still tied 0-0 at halftime. That group broke just once after a muffed kickoff put them in a bad spot, giving up a TD pass on fourth down to make it 7-0 CN at 9:32 of the third quarter.

Despite all the new looks offensively, Columbus was forced to punt eight times as South had eight tackles for loss and held the Bull Dogs to 102 yards, 46 rushing (on 25 carries) and five first downs.

"I feel like our effort was pretty good," lineman Donovan Avila said. "We definitely kept our ground even when things were starting to get tougher."

Good thing as for the first time all season, the Panthers, who came in averaging 53 ppg, needed a stout effort to save the day.

"I feel like it's just great coordination," Avila said. "Great teamwork too, overall. We just kept it together. Great composure."

That effort allowed a sputtering offense to find its footing.

"They've been great all season long," Combs said. "They've held teams to really low scores. They're getting us the ball with the interceptions. When we come off the field, we're going to be right back out there."

One of the things South did to pep up its offense was go into hurry-up mode behind its all-state QB no matter where they were on the field. Combs was key after a less than stellar first half with 76 yards passing and an interception in the end zone right before halftime.

Defensively, South kept attacking. Offensively, South was still getting stuck on too many third-and-long situation, but Combs started taking advantage of the field position and connecting with his receivers.

"They were loading the box, bringing blitzes to try and stop the run," Combs said. "Hayden's a great runner, so you've got to stop something. So we saw a chance behind the blitzes to take some shots over the middle, take some shots deep, and it started working out for us."

Following the Winstead TD, South forced a punt and South took is 74 yards, with Combs finding Mayson Lewis over the middle from 24 yards out on fourth and 8 at the 7:56 mark for some breathing room, 17-7.

Then an interception by Charlie Morris at the CN 40 set up an insurance score as Combs zipped a 13-yarder to Winstead with 4:10 left. Crisis averted.

"You've got to lean on your playmakers and eventually, they come through," Johnson said.

Winstead caught seven passes for 139 yards, Parker four for 34 and Lewis three for 61 as Combs threw for 234.

"It was a check who we were inside," Combs said. "It's what we want, toward the end of the season. We've got a tough schedule to finish it out. We want those tough games to prove once we get to the tournament, we're ready, we're ready for battles, all four quarters."

articles.title: Big plays, stout defense propel Brennan to blowout win against O'Connor
articles.summary: Aiden Martin made an impact on both sides of the ball as the Bears controlled the game from start to finish in a big District 29-6A win over the Panthers.
articles.body:
Since opening the season with a tough overtime loss against Austin Vandegrift, the Brennan Bears have been on a tear.

The latest example of their dominance occurred Friday night when they paired a quick-strike offense with a stout defense in a 44-0-victory against O'Connor at Farris Stadium.

In senior Aiden Martin's case, he showed out on both sides with a 46-yard touchdown on an end around coming out of the slot. He also factored in the Bears' efforts on defense in the secondary.

"It's amazing," Martin said. "The coaches are putting me in great positions to be successful, and so I really just have to deliver on it. The conditioning is a little different, but I had to get used to it after the first two games."

The No 4 Bears improved to 4-1 overall with their third shutout in the last four games. They are also 3-0 in District 29-6A. O'Connor dropped to 2-2 and 1-1.

Tenth-ranked Harlan is also 4-1 and 3-0 after downing Marshall 59-14 on Thursday. If history is any indication, the Bears and Hawks could be headed for a showdown for the district title in the final week. Since 2020, either Brennan or Harlan has won the district champion.

For now, the Bears are focused on building on the momentum from Friday's victory. After a 28-21 overtime loss against Vandegrift, the Bears posted wins against Reagan (63-0), Taft (56-7) and Sotomayor (49-0).

"Vandegrift was a great test," Martin said. "We saw the level we were at, and we were able to see our growth points - like tackling, finishing third down conversions. I'm extremely proud of our guys. Going into that next practice (after Vandegrift) we were extremely focused and we just had to get back."

They want that to continue over the second half of the season.

"Our mindset had to be that we've got to be humble all the time, no matter what," junior linebacker Johnas Brewster said. "No matter who we play. We've always got to humble."

As long as their playmakers produce, that shouldn't be a problem.

Nicholas Oliver Jr. returned a kickoff 58 yards for a touchdown to give the Bears a 9-0 lead midway through the first quarter. Martin's touchdown one minute into the second quarter put the Bears ahead 16-0.

Junior Jayshawn Mitchell, a rising national college recruit, caught a 66-yard touchdown pass from a scrambling Jeremiah Conwell with 1:16 left in the second quarter for a 23-0 halftime lead.

Mitchell added a 1-yard scoring run, and Oliver scored on a 23-yard touchdown catch in the second half.

Brewster was in on a host of tackles, including a pair for losses that led to a safety on a bad snap to the back of the end zone for a safety and a 2-0 lead with 6:33 in the first quarter.

The Bears yielded 169 yards, while gaining 461. Brennan kept the Panthers out the zone despite a couple of short fields.

"What was working well for us was our d-line," Brewster said. "They had a big push up front, and the backer had to come over and it. Everyone rallied to the ball. Eleven people to the ball, and we were playing with all our heart."

articles.title: What we learned in week 6 of Greater Cincinnati high school football
articles.summary: Here are the top highlights from a wild week 6 in Greater Cincinnati high school football.
articles.body:
Week 6 of the Greater Cincinnati high school football season brought some of the wildest results yet as road wins by several teams shook up conference races across the city.

In Northern Kentucky , the first week of district play brought a few exciting results as well.

Here's a recap of some of the top action in the tri-state.

St. Xavier stuns Elder, muddies the GCL-South race

As Owen Davidson's 26-yard field goal split the uprights and sailed into the Price Hill night, the St. Xavier Bombers stormed the field, celebrating a 31-29 win at The Pit, as well as head coach Steve Specht's 200th win .

"I don't know how many of our games have come down to the last play, it's been quite a few over my career and coach Ramsey's career. I'm just so proud of our kids, happy for them. I talked about it all week long, all of the sudden you're 2-3 and everybody's jumping off the bandwagon. I told them not to worry about it, it's always been about us. Focus on development, focus on getting better, and I couldn't be more proud of a group of young men," Specht said.

When the Bombers took the opening kickoff and marched 57 yards in nine plays, taking 5:01 off the clock, there was a tension in the air that St. X might actually leave Glenway Ave. with a win. Thomas George, the fourth different Bomber to take snaps under center this year, was as composed as he could be, completing 63.6 percent of his passes for 192 yards and three touchdowns. Aiden Graham posted a season-high 21 carries for 114 yards.

The Bombers went 7-for-11 in third-down conversions and converted their only fourth-down play, a 10-yard pass from George to Aidan Newdigate keeping the final drive alive.

"There wasn't one dude in that locker room that didn't believe this was gonna happen. Like coach Specht thought, we were gonna come in here and we were gonna win this game. It was a great opportunity," George said.

But Elder punched back every time it needed to. Quarterback Kaden Estep got it done on the ground and through the air, passing for 236 yards and three touchdowns and running for the go-ahead score with 5:10 left. Andrew Lyman, who was initially ruled ineligible but received a Temporary Restraining Order to play, caught four passes for 84 yards, including a 34-yard touchdown.

The defense made its lone stand early in the fourth quarter. After an Estep punt was downed at the 1-yard line, Pete Fortkamp jumped on George in the end zone for a safety, seemingly flipping the momentum. It was a blessing in disguise for the Bombers as they ended up getting the last laugh.

"Elder's a heck of a football team. Coach Ramsey does a great job. That offense - Kaden Estep is special, but we did just enough tonight to slow him down.," Specht said.

While St. X faces another daunting task next week with a trip to Louisville Trinity, it finishes the season with a favorable schedule against La Salle, Cleveland St. Ignatius and St. James Performance Academy (Washington, D.C.).

Elder will have a fire in its belly as it travels to face Moeller and Highlands (KY), then hosts Bishop Chatard (IN) and Mount Zion Prep (MD).

If Elder beats Moeller at Dayton's Welcome Stadium on Oct. 2 and St. Xavier beats La Salle on Oct. 9, the Bombers, Crusaders and Panthers will all have 2-1 league records and split the GCL-South title. It would be the first three-way tie since La Salle, Moeller and St. Xavier shared the title in 2014.

East Central rallies with running game, defense, to end Harrison's unbeaten start

East Central does not have an explosive passing game this year.

Trailing 21-7 at halftime at Harrison, and receiving the second-half kickoff, the Trojans needed a quick start to the second half to have a chance to win. They got that with their powerful running game, and got one big pass play when they needed it most, to edge Harrison, 24-21. Both teams left with 5-1 records in the battle of Interstate 74 between two schools about 12 miles apart.

Senior Ryan Minges rushed for 186 on 28 carries. Colton Bellman had 64 yards on 12 attempts and Chase Marsh 37 yards on six carries.

"It is definitely extremely special to have three backs," Minges said. "We have totally different run games and it's going to be hard for teams to stop it in the coming weeks."

Harrison took a 14-0 lead on two sustained drives, and led 21-7 at halftime after David Baldock returned an interception to midfield. Brady Lawhon rushed for two touchdowns and threw a TD pass to Kyle Davidson. But East Central shut down the Wildcats in the second half, allowing 207 yards for the game, most of that in the first half.

East Central scored from the second-half kickoff, driving 50 yards, all on the ground, and trailed 21-14 with 8:03 to go in the third quarter.

"We came into halftime knowing we didn't play our best," Minges said. "We all rallied together and knew the game wasn't over. We had to play four quarters and win the game. We set a goal at halftime that we had to come out and score, and the defense needed to get a big stop."

The Trojans came back to win in the fourth quarter with some clutch defense. Trailing 21-14 late in the third quarter, East Central stopped Harrison on fourth down in the red zone, and started to drive the other way.

Early in the fourth quarter, East Central tried a flea-flicker. Ben Bond threw a long pass to the goal line. The receiver slipped and a Harrison defender nearly intercepted the pass, which he had a chance to return for a touchdown. Bond converted a fourth-and-10 pass later on the drive, and Blake Sterwerf kicked a 35-yard field goal to make it 21-17 with 10:57 to go.

With seven minutes to go, Jared Cox intercepted Lawhon at the Harrison 35. EC drove down for a score, by Bellman with 3:55 to go, to lead 24-21.

Colton Rehage returned the kickoff to midfield. Lawhon threw a pass to the sideline to an open receiver, but was just a bit off and senior Noah Long made a leaping one-handed interception. EC ran out the clock from there.

East Central is top-ranked in Class 4A in the latest Indiana coaches poll.

Moeller evolving alongside sophomore QB McLaughlin

The Moeller Crusaders left no doubt in a dominant 45-0 showing against league-foe La Salle, earning themselves at least a share of the GCLS crown. What's perhaps more exciting for the Crusaders is the leaps and bounds of growth they're seeing from their new quarterback.

In just his second start for the Crusaders, sophomore signal-caller Hunter McLaughlin went 14-of-18 for 239 yards and three touchdowns in the first half against the Lancers, ending his day early with a 35-0 lead. Even without playing in Moeller's two losses, McLaughlin has thrown for 742 yards and eight touchdowns without an interception, completing over 72% of his passes.

"When he first got to us, the arm talent jumped. It was undeniable," Moeller head coach Bert Bathiany said. "There's a difference between being a good thrower and a being a good quarterback, and he's becoming a good quarterback."

After Moeller graduated former Ohio Mr. Football Matt Ponatoski last year, the quarterback room had big shoes to fill. McLaughlin is starting to look more comfortable in the role each week, and his play has elevated Moeller into true contenders in Cincinnati.

Of course, it's far from a one man show for Moeller. The defense strangled La Salle all night, allowing just 74 total yards and forcing a shutout. The Crusaders' stable of running backs combined for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 6.2 yards per carry, and the receiving corps consistently executed on deep routes and followed downfield blocks.

When asked about the ceiling for the Crusaders this season, McLaughlin had the utmost confidence in his squad.

"This team could make the state championship game."

For the first time since the 1981 Deer Park team went 10-0, the Wildcats have started a season with a 6-0 record. Deer Park beat Madeira 38-14 and star Morgan Brown broke the school's scoring record in the contest.

North College Hill undefeated and unscored on

North College Hill beat Dayton Belmont 61-0 on Sept. 24, improving to 5-0 for the year. The undefeated Trojans (who had their Week 1 game against Fairport Harding canceled) have yet to allow a point this season, outscoring opponents a combined 257-0.

Who are the top performers from week 6 of Greater Cincinnati high school football?

Lucas Cannady, St. Bernard-Elmwood Place: In a tough 38-26 loss to Summit Country Day, the senior quarterback threw for 265 yards and a touchdown and ran for 189 yards and three more scores.

Jordan Davis, Anderson: In a 58-14 blowout at Milford, he hauled in eight passes for 177 yards and an 80-yard touchdown.

Roman Garr, Colerain : He threw for 300 yards and five touchdowns in a 47-31 win over Oak Hills.

Thomas George, St. Xavier: In his first start at quarterback, he led the Bombers to a monumental win at Elder by throwing for 192 yards and three touchdowns.

Jordan Hall, Princeton: In a 48-22 win at Lakota East, Hall ran 15 times for 140 yards and four touchdowns.

Hunter McLaughlin, Moeller: The sophomore quarterback torched La Salle in one half of play, going 14-of-18 for 239 yards and three touchdowns in an eventual 45-0 win.

Kiyan Miller, Covington Catholic: The sophomore ran for four touchdowns as the Colonels defeated Louisville Central 41-14.

Alex Nagel, Mason: The Comets quarterback led Mason to a 40-3 win against Hamilton, completing a pair of passes, both for scores, while rushing for 118 yards and two more touchdowns.

Gavin Nolan, Middletown : He stepped in at QB and threw for 289 yards and four touchdowns while rushing for a TD, in a 40-0 win over Sycamore.

Kenyon Norman, Lakota West: The Northwestern commit has eclipsed the 1,000 rushing yard mark in six games after running 12 times for 101 yards and two touchdowns in a 38-7 win over Fairfield.

Callan Polland, Turpin: The junior hauled in five receptions, including all four of Turpin's passing scores, for 169 yards in Turpin's 55-19 win against West Clermont.

Owen Scalf, Anderson: Anderson had 469 passing yards in a 58-14 win at Milford, including a 26-for-30 night with 433 yards, five touchdowns and an interception from Scalf.

Will Schmittauer, Turpin: Turpin cruised to a 55-19 win against West Clermont with Schmittauer throwing for 368 yards and four touchdowns.

Jack Sills, Kings: The senior had a career game despite a 35-24 loss to Lebanon, completing 23 of his 34 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns.

Quinton Simon, Highlands: The sophomore defensive back and receiver returned two interceptions for touchdowns and ran in another on offense in a 78-6 win over Harrison County.

Key'Sean Torbert, Princeton: Torbert was 15-for-24 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown while amassing 130 rushing yards and a score in eight rushes as Princeton improved to 6-0 by beating Lakota East 48-22.

Nathan Tucker, Kings: In a 35-24 loss to Lebanon, Tucker caught five passes for 141 yards and a touchdown. Defensively, ha had an interception.
